 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 set -euo pipefail
 
 ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
 SKILL="$ROOT/work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous"
 HARNESS="$SKILL/templates/harness"
 
 fail() {
   echo "FAIL: $*" >&2
   exit 1
 }
 
 assert_contains() {
   local haystack="$1"
   local needle="$2"
   [[ "$haystack" == *"$needle"* ]] || fail "expected text to contain: $needle"
 }
 
 skill_dirs="$(find "$ROOT/work/skills" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | sort)"
 if [ "$skill_dirs" != "$SKILL" ]; then
   fail "work/skills must contain only flashdb-rust-autonomous"
 fi
 
 skill_files="$(find "$ROOT/work/skills" -name SKILL.md -type f | sort)"
 if [ "$skill_files" != "$SKILL/SKILL.md" ]; then
   fail "expected only work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/SKILL.md"
 fi
 
 for dir in \
   "$ROOT/.agent" "$ROOT/.agents" "$ROOT/.agent-handoff" \
   "$ROOT/config" "$ROOT/templates" "$ROOT/scripts" "$ROOT/tests" \
   "$ROOT/harness" "$ROOT/examples"
 do
   [ ! -e "$dir" ] || fail "root package should not contain $(basename "$dir")"
 done
 
 instruction_text="$(cat "$ROOT/INSTRUCTION.md")"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "# 执行入口"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/SKILL.md"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "Skill 名称：flashdb-rust-autonomous"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" '源项目固定为 `code/FlashDB`'
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" 'Rust 目标固定为 `code/flashDB_rust`'
-assert_contains "$instruction_text" "执行模型固定为 GLM 5.1"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "禁止使用 subagent 或 task agent"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "不询问用户，不中断执行"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" "失败就按 Skill 内的循环修复并重新验证"
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" 'work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/scripts/final_verify_target.sh'
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" 'result/output.md'
 assert_contains "$instruction_text" 'logs/trace'
 if printf '%s' "$instruction_text" | grep -Eqi 'opencode|c-to-rust|openspec|superpowers|评分规则|比赛'; then
   fail "INSTRUCTION.md must remain a tool-neutral direct skill entry"
 fi
 if [[ "$instruction_text" == *"不加载其它 skill"* || "$instruction_text" == *"Do not load any other skill"* ]]; then
   fail "INSTRUCTION.md should not emphasize loading no other skills"
 fi
 
 skill_text="$(cat "$SKILL/SKILL.md")"
 for needle in \
   "references/c-to-rust-translation-spec.md" \
   "references/source-manifest.sha256" \
   "scripts/final_verify_target.sh" \
   "C-Test-First Translation" \
   "c_coverage_check.py --progress" \
   "api_surface_check.py --progress" \
   "translation_spec_check.py --progress" \
   "evidence_runner.py" \
   "trace_capture.py" \
   "c_interop_test.sh" \
   "ready_for_final" \
   "result/output.md" \
   "POSIX file mode" \
   "FDB_WRITE_GRAN=1"
 do
   assert_contains "$skill_text" "$needle"
 done
 
 cargo_template="$(cat "$SKILL/templates/Cargo.toml")"
 assert_contains "$cargo_template" 'crate-type = ["rlib", "staticlib"]'
 
 spec_file="$SKILL/references/c-to-rust-translation-spec.md"
 manifest="$SKILL/references/source-manifest.sha256"
 [ -s "$spec_file" ] || fail "missing Chinese C-to-Rust specification"
 [ -s "$manifest" ] || fail "missing source hash manifest"
 spec_text="$(cat "$spec_file")"
 for rule_id in \
   BASE-01 PROF-01 IMM-01 COV-01 API-01 TDD-01 INT-01 LAY-01 \
   STA-01 PST-01 XIO-01 ABI-01 MEM-01 ERR-01 CBK-01 GLB-01 EVD-01 LOG-01 VER-01
 do
   assert_contains "$spec_text" "$rule_id"
 done
 assert_contains "$spec_text" "必须采用 C 测试优先"
 assert_contains "$spec_text" "公开 API 必须逐项闭合"
 assert_contains "$spec_text" "必须验证 C 与 Rust 双向持久化兼容"
 assert_contains "$spec_text" "证据必须绑定当前输入和当前实现"
 assert_contains "$spec_text" "AI 交互和验证日志必须完整留存"
 
 required_files=(
   "$SKILL/templates/Cargo.toml"
   "$SKILL/templates/cargo-config.toml"
   "$SKILL/references/c-to-rust-translation-spec.md"
   "$SKILL/references/source-manifest.sha256"
   "$SKILL/scripts/final_verify_target.sh"
   "$SKILL/scripts/self_check.sh"
   "$SKILL/tests/trace_capture_test.py"
   "$HARNESS/preflight.sh"
   "$HARNESS/build_check.sh"
   "$HARNESS/test_all.sh"
   "$HARNESS/c_link_test.sh"
   "$HARNESS/c_interop_test.sh"
   "$HARNESS/unsafe_audit.sh"
   "$HARNESS/final_verify.sh"
   "$HARNESS/c_coverage_check.py"
   "$HARNESS/api_surface_check.py"
   "$HARNESS/translation_spec_check.py"
   "$HARNESS/config_profile_check.py"
   "$HARNESS/evidence_runner.py"
   "$HARNESS/trace_capture.py"
   "$HARNESS/checkpoint.py"
   "$HARNESS/rust_policy_check.py"
   "$HARNESS/source_guard.py"
   "$HARNESS/interop/interop_driver.c"
 )
 for file in "${required_files[@]}"; do
   [ -s "$file" ] || fail "missing or empty skill asset: ${file#$ROOT/}"
 done
 
 for script in "$HARNESS"/*.sh "$SKILL/scripts"/*.sh "$SKILL/tests"/*.sh; do
   [ -x "$script" ] || fail "script must be executable: ${script#$ROOT/}"
   bash -n "$script" || fail "invalid shell syntax: ${script#$ROOT/}"
 done
 
 python3 -m py_compile "$HARNESS"/*.py
 python3 "$SKILL/tests/trace_capture_test.py"
 rm -rf "$HARNESS/__pycache__" "$SKILL/tests/__pycache__"
 
 "${CC:-cc}" -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra \
   -I"$ROOT/code/FlashDB/tests" -I"$ROOT/code/FlashDB/inc" -I"$ROOT/code/FlashDB/src" \
   "$HARNESS/interop/interop_driver.c"
 
 python3 - "$ROOT" "$manifest" <<'PY'
 import hashlib
 import pathlib
 import sys
 
 root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
 manifest = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
 expected = {}
 for line in manifest.read_text().splitlines():
     if line.strip():
         digest, relative = line.split(None, 1)
         expected[relative.strip()] = digest
 
 actual = set()
 for directory in [root / "code/FlashDB/inc", root / "code/FlashDB/src", root / "code/FlashDB/tests"]:
     for path in directory.rglob("*"):
         if path.is_file() and (path.suffix in {".c", ".h"} or path.name == "Makefile"):
             actual.add(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
 if actual != set(expected):
     raise SystemExit("source manifest file set mismatch")
 for relative, digest in expected.items():
     if hashlib.sha256((root / relative).read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
         raise SystemExit(f"source manifest hash mismatch: {relative}")
 PY
 
 final_text="$(cat "$HARNESS/final_verify.sh")"
 for needle in \
   "source_guard.py" "preflight.sh" "test_all.sh" "c_link_test.sh" \
   "c_interop_test.sh" "c_coverage_check.py" "api_surface_check.py" \
   "trace_capture.py verify" "translation_spec_check.py" \
   "checkpoint.py verify-final" "rust_policy_check.py"
 do
   assert_contains "$final_text" "$needle"
 done
 if grep -Rq "RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP" "$HARNESS"; then
   fail "fixed harness must not depend on RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP"
 fi
 
 echo "package_check.sh: PASS"

# Transpilot FlashDB Competition Package

This repository is packaged for one task: translate FlashDB from C to Rust with
OpenCode.

## Entry

Use the repository root entry file:

```text
INSTRUCTION.md
```

It tells OpenCode to load and execute:

```text
work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/SKILL.md
```

`transpilot init` is not a skill and is not part of this competition package.

## Fixed Task

- Source: `code/FlashDB`
- Target: `code/flashDB_rust`
- Skill name: `flashdb-rust-autonomous`
- Final gate: `code/flashDB_rust/harness/final_verify.sh`
- Result file: `result/output.md`

The skill owns the full loop: source inspection, Rust design, implementation,
test porting, repair, final verification, and result update. Fixed target
harness scripts are prebuilt under the skill and copied into
`code/flashDB_rust/harness/` during Phase 0.

## Directory Layout

```text
transpilot/
├── INSTRUCTION.md
├── AGENTS.md
├── code/
│   └── FlashDB/
├── work/
│   └── skills/
│       └── flashdb-rust-autonomous/
│           ├── SKILL.md
│           ├── scripts/
│           │   └── self_check.sh
│           ├── templates/
│           │   ├── Cargo.toml
│           │   ├── cargo-config.toml
│           │   └── harness/
│           └── tests/
│               └── package_check.sh
├── result/
│   └── output.md
├── logs/
└── docs/
```

## Local Checks

The repository-level checks for this package are:

```bash
work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/scripts/self_check.sh
```

`code/flashDB_rust` is created and completed by the skill during the OpenCode
competition run. Once present, the required final verification command is:

```bash
cd code/flashDB_rust && ./harness/final_verify.sh
```

1: ---
2: name: flashdb-rust-autonomous
3: description: Autonomously translate code/FlashDB to code/flashDB_rust with C-test-first development, source-bound evidence, C ABI compatibility, and bidirectional persistence verification.
4: ---
5: 
6: # FlashDB Rust Autonomous Translation
7: 
8: ## Fixed Contract
9: 
10: - C source: `code/FlashDB`
11: - Rust target: `code/flashDB_rust`
12: - Crate and static library name: `flashdb_rust`
13: - Release library: `code/flashDB_rust/target/release/libflashdb_rust.a`
14: - Supported profile: POSIX file mode, KVDB and TSDB enabled,
15:   `FDB_WRITE_GRAN=1`, signed 32-bit timestamp
16: - Trusted completion command:
17:   `work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/scripts/final_verify_target.sh`
18: - Result file: `result/output.md`
19: - Complete AI interaction and verification trace: `logs/trace/`
20: 
21: Do not ask the user questions. Keep inspecting, testing, implementing, and
22: repairing until the trusted completion command passes and the result file is
23: updated.
24: 
25: Read `references/c-to-rust-translation-spec.md` completely before changing the
26: target. It is mandatory for design, implementation, testing, and verification.
27: The scripts are enforcement tools, not a replacement for understanding C.
28: 
29: ## Trust Boundary
30: 
31: During translation:
32: 
33: - do not edit files under `code/FlashDB`; compiler objects and temporary test
34:   output are allowed, but C source, headers, tests, and Makefiles are immutable;
35: - do not edit `INSTRUCTION.md` or anything under
36:   `work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous`;
37: - do not weaken, skip, replace, or locally patch a harness check;
38: - never use the current Rust behavior as the oracle for a Rust test;
39: - never claim success from a report row, process exit alone, or a worker result.
40: 
41: `references/source-manifest.sha256` binds the accepted C input. The trusted
42: launcher checks both the source manifest and the copied target harness before
43: and after final verification.
44: 
45: ## Autonomous Loop
46: 
47: Use one main-agent loop:
48: 
49: ```text
50: preflight and restore checkpoint
51:   -> inspect the next C case or public API item
52:   -> record a C-derived oracle
53:   -> add the Rust acceptance test first
54:   -> observe the focused test fail for the missing behavior
55:   -> implement the smallest source-equivalent behavior
56:   -> run the focused test and progressive gates
57:   -> record source-bound evidence and checkpoint
58:   -> repeat until all queues are closed
59:   -> freeze Rust source and rebuild final evidence
60:   -> run the trusted completion command
61:   -> update result/output.md and run the trusted command again
62: ```
63: 
64: For a behavior failure, never stop after a fixed retry count. After three
65: failures with the same approach, change the approach: reduce the slice, add a C
66: probe, inspect a lower-level call path, or replace the implementation strategy.
67: 
68: An environment blocker is different from a behavior failure. If preflight exits
69: with code `2`, retry the exact blocker after one repair attempt. Only when the
70: same external blocker occurs three consecutive times may execution stop. Record
71: the command, three logs, and required external action in `result/output.md` with
72: status `BLOCKED`. Missing tools, unreadable fixed source, unwritable workspace,
73: or exhausted disk are blockers; failing builds and tests are not.
74: 
75: ## Phase 0: Install Fixed Harness
76: 
77: From the repository root, create or resume the target and replace only its
78: harness with the fixed template:
79: 
80: ```bash
81: SKILL_DIR="work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous"
82: TARGET="code/flashDB_rust"
83: mkdir -p "$TARGET/.cargo" "$TARGET/src" "$TARGET/tests" "$TARGET/reports"
84: cp "$SKILL_DIR/templates/cargo-config.toml" "$TARGET/.cargo/config.toml"
85: if [ ! -f "$TARGET/Cargo.toml" ]; then
86:   cp "$SKILL_DIR/templates/Cargo.toml" "$TARGET/Cargo.toml"
87: fi
88: python3 - "$SKILL_DIR" "$TARGET" <<'PY'
89: import pathlib
90: import shutil
91: import sys
92: 
93: skill = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
94: target = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
95: destination = target / "harness"
96: if destination.exists():
97:     shutil.rmtree(destination)
98: shutil.copytree(skill / "templates/harness", destination)
99: PY
100: chmod +x "$TARGET/harness/"*.sh
101: ```
102: 
103: Do not delete valid Rust implementation work when resuming. The fixed
104: `.cargo/config.toml` must deny warnings, and `Cargo.toml` must contain:
105: 
106: ```toml
107: [lib]
108: name = "flashdb_rust"
109: path = "src/lib.rs"
110: crate-type = ["rlib", "staticlib"]
111: ```
112: 
113: Initialize and validate the queues:
114: 
115: ```bash
116: cd code/flashDB_rust
117: python3 harness/source_guard.py --target .
118: ./harness/preflight.sh
119: python3 harness/checkpoint.py init
120: python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --init
121: python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --init
122: python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --init
123: python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --progress
124: python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --progress
125: python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --progress
126: ```
127: 
128: The three `--init` commands reconcile current required rows, preserve valid
129: current work, and remove stale rows. They do not turn unfinished rows into
130: passes.
131: 
132: ## Phase 1: Source Design and C Oracle
133: 
134: Create or refresh these target reports from C source evidence:
135: 
136: - `reports/source-inventory.md`: every C source/header/test, size, includes,
137:   key public and static symbols, module dependencies, translation order;
138: - `reports/config-profile.md`: output of `config_profile_check.py`;
139: - `reports/layout-probe.md`: measured C sizes, alignments, offsets, endian and
140:   write-granularity facts;
141: - `reports/c-oracle-traces/`: original C test and focused C probe output;
142: - `reports/progress.md`: checkpoint, current queue item, latest command, next
143:   action.
144: 
145: Use this dependency order unless source evidence proves otherwise:
146: 
147: 1. configuration, types, constants, status tables, alignment, layout;
148: 2. `fdb_utils.c` CRC and low-level helpers;
149: 3. `fdb_file.c` POSIX storage backend;
150: 4. `fdb.c` shared initialization/deinitialization;
151: 5. `fdb_kvdb.c` KV state machine and recovery;
152: 6. `fdb_tsdb.c` time-series state machine and recovery;
153: 7. C ABI, controls, callbacks, iteration, output, and all C test cases.
154: 
155: Run the original C suite before translating behavior and save its complete
156: output as an oracle trace. If the original suite cannot run, build a focused C
157: probe for the affected behavior and save its source, compile command, and
158: output. A static oracle must cite the exact C file, function, branch, macro, and
159: expected value.
160: 
161: The required work queues are:
162: 
163: - `reports/c-test-coverage-required.tsv`: every `TEST_RUN(...)` occurrence;
164: - `reports/c-api-required.tsv`: every public function and KVDB/TSDB control;
165: - `reports/c-module-coverage.tsv`: every C source module;
166: - `reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv`: every Chinese specification rule.
167: 
168: ## Phase 2: C-Test-First Translation
169: 
170: For each row in `c-test-coverage-required.tsv`, in file order:
171: 
172: 1. Read the complete C test body, helpers, macros, and production call path.
173: 2. Record the exact case id, such as
174:    `fdb_kvdb_tc.c::test_fdb_kvdb_init#1`.
175: 3. Run the original C case or focused probe where needed.
176: 4. Add one distinct Rust `#[test]` under `tests/c_kvdb_cases.rs` or
177:    `tests/c_tsdb_cases.rs` before changing production Rust.
178: 5. Put the exact C case id inside the test body and reproduce C setup,
179:    operation order, assertions, restart context, and expected values.
180: 6. Run the focused Rust test and confirm it fails for the missing behavior.
181: 7. Implement the smallest equivalent behavior in the safe Rust core and narrow
182:    FFI boundary.
183: 8. Run the focused test successfully through `evidence_runner.py`.
184: 9. Add its `reports/evidence/*.json` path to the coverage row and update the
185:    checkpoint.
186: 
187: Example successful focused-test evidence:
188: 
189: ```bash
190: python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run \
191:   --id ccase-kvdb-init-1 -- \
192:   cargo test --release test_fdb_kvdb_init_first_pass -- --exact --nocapture
193: ```
194: 
195: The coverage row's `oracle` must name the exact C test file and function. Its
196: `evidence` must reference successful structured evidence for that exact Rust
197: test. Repeated C cases require distinct Rust tests and distinct evidence.
198: 
199: After each slice run:
200: 
201: ```bash
202: cargo fmt
203: ./harness/build_check.sh
204: ./harness/test_all.sh
205: python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --progress
206: python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --progress
207: python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --progress
208: python3 harness/rust_policy_check.py
209: ```
210: 
211: After any C ABI, persistent-format, callback, control, or iterator change, also
212: run:
213: 
214: ```bash
215: ./harness/c_link_test.sh
216: ./harness/c_interop_test.sh
217: ```
218: 
219: Update `reports/progress.md` and record the case and last successful command:
220: 
221: ```bash
222: python3 harness/checkpoint.py record \
223:   --case '<case-id>' --stage slice_passed \
224:   --command '<focused command>' --exit-code 0
225: ```
226: 
227: ## Mandatory Semantic Areas
228: 
229: Closing the C test queue alone is insufficient. The implementation must also
230: close every row in the public API, module, and specification queues.
231: 
232: The following are mandatory:
233: 
234: - exact persistent byte layout, status transitions, CRC, erased values,
235:   padding, sector movement, GC, recovery, and restart behavior;
236: - all public symbols from `inc/flashdb.h` exported by the release static
237:   library with exact C signatures;
238: - every KVDB/TSDB control command, including lock/unlock callbacks, getters,
239:   rollover, file mode, max size, and not-formatable mode;

---
name: flashdb-rust-autonomous
description: Autonomously translate code/FlashDB to code/flashDB_rust with C-test-first development, source-bound evidence, C ABI compatibility, and bidirectional persistence verification.
---

# FlashDB Rust Autonomous Translation

## Fixed Contract

- C source: `code/FlashDB`
- Rust target: `code/flashDB_rust`
- Crate and static library name: `flashdb_rust`
- Release library: `code/flashDB_rust/target/release/libflashdb_rust.a`
- Supported profile: POSIX file mode, KVDB and TSDB enabled,
  `FDB_WRITE_GRAN=1`, signed 32-bit timestamp
- Trusted completion command:
  `work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/scripts/final_verify_target.sh`
- Result file: `result/output.md`
- Complete AI interaction and verification trace: `logs/trace/`

Do not ask the user questions. Keep inspecting, testing, implementing, and
repairing until the trusted completion command passes and the result file is
updated.

Read `references/c-to-rust-translation-spec.md` completely before changing the
target. It is mandatory for design, implementation, testing, and verification.
The scripts are enforcement tools, not a replacement for understanding C.

## Trust Boundary

During translation:

- do not edit files under `code/FlashDB`; compiler objects and temporary test
  output are allowed, but C source, headers, tests, and Makefiles are immutable;
- do not edit `INSTRUCTION.md` or anything under
  `work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous`;
- do not weaken, skip, replace, or locally patch a harness check;
- never use the current Rust behavior as the oracle for a Rust test;
- never claim success from a report row, process exit alone, or a worker result.

`references/source-manifest.sha256` binds the accepted C input. The trusted
launcher checks both the source manifest and the copied target harness before
and after final verification.

## Autonomous Loop

Use one main-agent loop:

```text
preflight and restore checkpoint
  -> inspect the next C case or public API item
  -> record a C-derived oracle
  -> add the Rust acceptance test first
  -> observe the focused test fail for the missing behavior
  -> implement the smallest source-equivalent behavior
  -> run the focused test and progressive gates
  -> record source-bound evidence and checkpoint
  -> repeat until all queues are closed
  -> freeze Rust source and rebuild final evidence
  -> run the trusted completion command
  -> update result/output.md and run the trusted command again
```

For a behavior failure, never stop after a fixed retry count. After three
failures with the same approach, change the approach: reduce the slice, add a C
probe, inspect a lower-level call path, or replace the implementation strategy.

An environment blocker is different from a behavior failure. If preflight exits
with code `2`, retry the exact blocker after one repair attempt. Only when the
same external blocker occurs three consecutive times may execution stop. Record
the command, three logs, and required external action in `result/output.md` with
status `BLOCKED`. Missing tools, unreadable fixed source, unwritable workspace,
or exhausted disk are blockers; failing builds and tests are not.

## Phase 0: Install Fixed Harness

From the repository root, create or resume the target and replace only its
harness with the fixed template:

```bash
SKILL_DIR="work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous"
TARGET="code/flashDB_rust"
mkdir -p "$TARGET/.cargo" "$TARGET/src" "$TARGET/tests" "$TARGET/reports"
cp "$SKILL_DIR/templates/cargo-config.toml" "$TARGET/.cargo/config.toml"
if [ ! -f "$TARGET/Cargo.toml" ]; then
  cp "$SKILL_DIR/templates/Cargo.toml" "$TARGET/Cargo.toml"
fi
python3 - "$SKILL_DIR" "$TARGET" <<'PY'
import pathlib
import shutil
import sys

skill = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
target = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
destination = target / "harness"
if destination.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(destination)
shutil.copytree(skill / "templates/harness", destination)
PY
chmod +x "$TARGET/harness/"*.sh
```

Do not delete valid Rust implementation work when resuming. The fixed
`.cargo/config.toml` must deny warnings, and `Cargo.toml` must contain:

```toml
[lib]
name = "flashdb_rust"
path = "src/lib.rs"
crate-type = ["rlib", "staticlib"]
```

Initialize and validate the queues:

```bash
cd code/flashDB_rust
python3 harness/source_guard.py --target .
./harness/preflight.sh
python3 harness/checkpoint.py init
python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --init
python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --init
python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --init
python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --progress
python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --progress
python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --progress
```

The three `--init` commands reconcile current required rows, preserve valid
current work, and remove stale rows. They do not turn unfinished rows into
passes.

## Phase 1: Source Design and C Oracle

Create or refresh these target reports from C source evidence:

- `reports/source-inventory.md`: every C source/header/test, size, includes,
  key public and static symbols, module dependencies, translation order;
- `reports/config-profile.md`: output of `config_profile_check.py`;
- `reports/layout-probe.md`: measured C sizes, alignments, offsets, endian and
  write-granularity facts;
- `reports/c-oracle-traces/`: original C test and focused C probe output;
- `reports/progress.md`: checkpoint, current queue item, latest command, next
  action.

Use this dependency order unless source evidence proves otherwise:

1. configuration, types, constants, status tables, alignment, layout;
2. `fdb_utils.c` CRC and low-level helpers;
3. `fdb_file.c` POSIX storage backend;
4. `fdb.c` shared initialization/deinitialization;
5. `fdb_kvdb.c` KV state machine and recovery;
6. `fdb_tsdb.c` time-series state machine and recovery;
7. C ABI, controls, callbacks, iteration, output, and all C test cases.

Run the original C suite before translating behavior and save its complete
output as an oracle trace. If the original suite cannot run, build a focused C
probe for the affected behavior and save its source, compile command, and
output. A static oracle must cite the exact C file, function, branch, macro, and
expected value.

The required work queues are:

- `reports/c-test-coverage-required.tsv`: every `TEST_RUN(...)` occurrence;
- `reports/c-api-required.tsv`: every public function and KVDB/TSDB control;
- `reports/c-module-coverage.tsv`: every C source module;
- `reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv`: every Chinese specification rule.

## Phase 2: C-Test-First Translation

For each row in `c-test-coverage-required.tsv`, in file order:

1. Read the complete C test body, helpers, macros, and production call path.
2. Record the exact case id, such as
   `fdb_kvdb_tc.c::test_fdb_kvdb_init#1`.
3. Run the original C case or focused probe where needed.
4. Add one distinct Rust `#[test]` under `tests/c_kvdb_cases.rs` or
   `tests/c_tsdb_cases.rs` before changing production Rust.
5. Put the exact C case id inside the test body and reproduce C setup,
   operation order, assertions, restart context, and expected values.
6. Run the focused Rust test and confirm it fails for the missing behavior.
7. Implement the smallest equivalent behavior in the safe Rust core and narrow
   FFI boundary.
8. Run the focused test successfully through `evidence_runner.py`.
9. Add its `reports/evidence/*.json` path to the coverage row and update the
   checkpoint.

Example successful focused-test evidence:

```bash
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run \
  --id ccase-kvdb-init-1 -- \
  cargo test --release test_fdb_kvdb_init_first_pass -- --exact --nocapture
```

The coverage row's `oracle` must name the exact C test file and function. Its
`evidence` must reference successful structured evidence for that exact Rust
test. Repeated C cases require distinct Rust tests and distinct evidence.

After each slice run:

```bash
cargo fmt
./harness/build_check.sh
./harness/test_all.sh
python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py --progress
python3 harness/api_surface_check.py --progress
python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py --progress
python3 harness/rust_policy_check.py
```

After any C ABI, persistent-format, callback, control, or iterator change, also
run:

```bash
./harness/c_link_test.sh
./harness/c_interop_test.sh
```

Update `reports/progress.md` and record the case and last successful command:

```bash
python3 harness/checkpoint.py record \
  --case '<case-id>' --stage slice_passed \
  --command '<focused command>' --exit-code 0
```

## Mandatory Semantic Areas

Closing the C test queue alone is insufficient. The implementation must also
close every row in the public API, module, and specification queues.

The following are mandatory:

- exact persistent byte layout, status transitions, CRC, erased values,
  padding, sector movement, GC, recovery, and restart behavior;
- all public symbols from `inc/flashdb.h` exported by the release static
  library with exact C signatures;
- every KVDB/TSDB control command, including lock/unlock callbacks, getters,
  rollover, file mode, max size, and not-formatable mode;
- callback invocation count, ordering, early stop, user context, and lock
  balance;
- real behavior for integrity checking, printing, iteration, reverse
  iteration, status updates, cleanup, and capacity calculations;
- error-code distinctions and output-parameter behavior;
- panic containment at every C ABI entry;
- no `static mut`, production `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic`, unfinished macro,
  placeholder path, or unjustified `unsafe`;
- C-produced databases readable by Rust, Rust-produced databases readable by
  C, and byte-identical deterministic KVDB/TSDB fixtures.

`harness/c_interop_test.sh` is the fixed cross-implementation gate. It must not
be replaced by a Rust-only round trip or by C tests whose writer and reader both
link the Rust implementation.

## Phase 3: Freeze and Rebuild Evidence

Structured evidence is bound to the current C source hash and current Rust
Cargo files, build configuration, `src/`, and `tests/` hash. Any later Rust
source, test, or build-input change makes old evidence stale. Once all behavior
is implemented:

1. Run `cargo fmt` and stop changing Rust source/tests.
2. Regenerate successful focused `cargo test` evidence for every C coverage
   row.
3. Generate final build, source guard, profile, C link, interop, and Rust policy
   evidence with `evidence_runner.py`.
4. Update API/module rows with the relevant C link or interop evidence.
5. Run strict C coverage and API checks through `evidence_runner.py`.
6. Update every compliance row with evidence whose command matches that rule.
7. Run the strict specification check.

Recommended final evidence commands:

```bash
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-source -- python3 harness/source_guard.py --target .
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-profile -- python3 harness/config_profile_check.py
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-build -- ./harness/build_check.sh
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-c-link -- ./harness/c_link_test.sh
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-interop -- ./harness/c_interop_test.sh
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-rust-policy -- python3 harness/rust_policy_check.py
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-c-coverage -- python3 harness/c_coverage_check.py
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-api -- python3 harness/api_surface_check.py
python3 harness/trace_capture.py export --target .
python3 harness/evidence_runner.py run --id final-trace -- python3 harness/trace_capture.py verify --target .
python3 harness/translation_spec_check.py
```

Evidence records live under `reports/evidence/`. A `PASS` ledger row without a
valid structured record is a failure. Do not manually fabricate JSON or logs.
Use `reports/evidence/final-trace.json` for `LOG-01`.

After all strict checks pass, record readiness:

```bash
python3 harness/checkpoint.py record \
  --case all --stage ready_for_final \
  --command 'strict pre-final gates' --exit-code 0
```

## Phase 4: Trusted Completion

Run from the repository root:

```bash
work/skills/flashdb-rust-autonomous/scripts/final_verify_target.sh
```

The trusted launcher automatically exports the latest active OpenCode session
for this repository, without `--sanitize`, to `logs/trace/llm_chat_log.json`.
It also snapshots the machine-generated verification JSON and raw logs under
`logs/trace/verification/` before rerunning every code-level gate. The trace is
an audit record only; statements in it never satisfy a gate.

If any command fails, return to the exact failed queue item, repair it, freeze
again, and regenerate stale evidence. Do not report partial completion.

After the trusted command passes, update `result/output.md`:

```markdown
## Execution Result

- Status: COMPLETED
- Source: code/FlashDB (C)
- Target: code/flashDB_rust (Rust)
- Supported profile: POSIX file mode, KVDB+TSDB, FDB_WRITE_GRAN=1, 32-bit timestamp
- Trusted final verification: PASSED
- Date: <current date>

### Verification Summary
- C-derived Rust cases: <passed>/<required>
- Public C API items: <passed>/<required>
- Original C-linked tests: PASSED
- C/Rust bidirectional persistence: PASSED
- Rust safety policy: PASSED
- Placeholders: NONE
```

Then run the trusted command once more. Only the second pass permits a final
success response.

## Subagent Policy

Do not delegate implementation or queue ownership. The main agent must continue
working and must remain responsible for all edits and verification.

A subagent may be used only for a read-only review of one named C function when
the platform can enforce a hard timeout of at most 10 minutes. Record start,
deadline, result, and acceptance in `reports/progress.md`. At timeout, abandon
the subagent and continue immediately. A subagent statement is never evidence
and never completion.

53: ## INT-01 保持 C 的整数和位运算语义
54: 
55: - 必须核对每个持久化字段、地址、长度、时间戳、状态位和 CRC 的 C 类型宽度及有无符号属性。
56: - 必须显式处理整数提升、截断、溢出、移位、按位取反和符号转换；不能依赖隐式 `as` 转换掩盖边界。
57: - 地址和磁盘格式字段应保持固定宽度类型，在切片索引边界经过检查后才能转换为 `usize`。
58: - 对齐、状态表大小和记录长度必须由与 C 宏等价的公式计算，禁止使用只对当前样本成立的常数。
59: 
60: ## LAY-01 磁盘格式按字节布局实现
61: 
62: - FlashDB 持久化结构必须视为字节协议，使用显式偏移和小端读写函数；禁止直接序列化普通 Rust 结构体。
63: - 只有真实 FFI 参数结构才能使用 `#[repr(C)]`，且必须用 C 布局探针验证大小、对齐和字段偏移。
64: - 必须验证 KVDB sector header、KV header、TSDB sector header、TSL index 的大小和关键偏移。
65: - 必须保持擦除值、写粒度、padding、magic、CRC 覆盖范围以及状态位在介质上的实际编码。
66: 
67: ## STA-01 状态机和遍历顺序必须等价
68: 
69: - sector、KV、TSL、GC 和迭代器必须按 C 的合法状态及转换条件实现，不能只保留最终业务值。
70: - 状态更新顺序必须保留掉电语义；禁止把多步单向写入折叠为一次高层集合更新。
71: - 必须覆盖空库、满 sector、跨 sector、重复写、删除后查找、GC 搬移、清理和重复初始化。
72: - 查询、遍历、回调和停止条件的顺序必须与 C 一致。
73: 
74: ## PST-01 持久化和重启语义必须可验证
75: 
76: - 文件后端和内存后端应通过同一核心行为接口，例如 `FlashBackend`，但不得改变 C 可观察行为。
77: - 必须测试关闭后重新打开、部分状态恢复、删除状态恢复、GC 后恢复和 TSDB 时间顺序恢复。
78: - 禁止仅在进程内维护权威映射而忽略介质扫描；若使用缓存，介质数据必须仍能独立恢复状态。
79: - 读写、擦除和边界失败必须沿调用链返回，不得静默成功。
80: 
81: ## XIO-01 必须验证 C 与 Rust 双向持久化兼容
82: 
83: - 必须使用同一份 C 调用驱动分别链接原 C 实现和 Rust 静态库，不能用两套不同测试逻辑比较结果。
84: - 必须验证 C 写入的 KVDB/TSDB 可由 Rust 重启读取，Rust 写入的数据库可由 C 重启读取。
85: - 对确定性输入，双方生成的 sector 文件必须逐字节一致；只比较业务返回值不足以证明格式兼容。
86: - 双向验证必须覆盖二进制 blob、固定时间戳、迭代顺序、控制 getter、锁/解锁平衡和可观察打印输出。
87: 
88: ## ABI-01 C ABI 必须精确兼容
89: 
90: - 原 C 测试使用到的公开符号必须由 release 静态库导出，并能由原头文件声明直接编译和链接。
91: - FFI 函数必须使用 `extern "C"`、稳定符号名和与 C 声明一致的参数/返回类型；需要时使用 `#[repr(C)]`。
92: - 指针的空值、长度、生命周期、别名和可写性必须在边界检查，内部立即转换为安全 Rust 表达。
93: - Rust panic 不得跨越 FFI 边界；边界必须转换为 C 能识别的错误码或失败结果。
94: - C 分配/C 释放、Rust 分配/Rust 释放不得交叉错配。
95: 
96: ## MEM-01 默认使用安全 Rust
97: 
98: - 所有权数据使用 `Vec<u8>` 或固定数组，借用数据使用切片，可空语义使用 `Option`，错误使用 `Result`。
99: - 每次地址加法、长度相加、切片范围和指针转切片都必须先检查溢出与边界。
100: - 禁止 `static mut`；共享可变状态必须使用锁、原子类型或线程局部状态，并保持 C 的生命周期语义。
101: - `unsafe` 只能位于不可避免的 FFI 或底层边界，范围必须最小，并在附近写明安全前提。
102: - 禁止在生产代码中使用 `unwrap()`、`expect()`、`todo!()`、`unimplemented!()` 或占位实现。
103: 
104: ## ERR-01 错误和输出参数语义必须保留
105: 
106: - 必须建立 C 错误码与 Rust 错误类型的完整映射，保留成功、未找到、无空间、读取失败、写入失败、校验失败等差异。
107: - C 输出参数只有在源实现会写入时才可修改；失败时是否保留旧值必须以 C 行为为准。
108: - 内部可以把输出参数改为 `Result<T, FdbErr>` 或 `Option<T>`，但 FFI 边界必须还原 C 调用约定。
109: - 禁止吞掉后端错误、用默认值代替错误或把不同错误统一成成功/未找到。
110: 
111: ## CBK-01 回调和控制参数必须类型化且保持调用契约
112: 
113: - flash 回调应在安全核心中建模为 trait 方法，`void *` 控制参数应转换为有类型的枚举或结构。
114: - 必须保留回调调用次数、顺序、停止条件、用户上下文和回调返回值对控制流的影响。
115: - FFI 回调保存时间不得超过 C 生命周期保证；禁止长期持有未经证明有效的裸指针。
116: - 可选回调和空上下文必须显式建模，不能用伪地址或全局可变变量替代。
117: 
118: ## GLB-01 全局状态、重入和并发边界必须明确
119: 
120: - 必须盘点 C 全局/静态状态，区分库状态、数据库实例状态和测试计数器。
121: - 实例状态必须归属对应 Rust 对象；测试计数器可使用 `thread_local!` 与 `Cell`，不得污染其他测试。
122: - 若 C 实现不保证线程安全，Rust 不得虚假宣称线程安全；若暴露 `Send`/`Sync`，必须有类型与同步证据。
123: - 初始化、反初始化、重复初始化和多实例互不干扰必须有测试。
124: 
125: ## EVD-01 证据必须绑定当前输入和当前实现
126: 
127: - 成功证据必须由固定运行器生成 JSON 和日志，记录命令、退出码、时间、日志哈希、C 输入哈希和 Rust 目标哈希。
128: - 修改 `Cargo.toml`、`src/` 或 `tests/` 后，此前证据全部失效，必须冻结实现后重新运行。
129: - C case 行必须绑定包含准确 Rust 测试名的聚焦 `cargo test` 命令；API、模块和规范行必须绑定对应门禁命令。
130: - 禁止手写证据 JSON、复用失败日志、引用不存在的路径，或用自然语言 `PASS` 代替可校验证据。
131: 
132: ## LOG-01 AI 交互和验证日志必须完整留存
133: 
134: - 必须把当前项目的完整 OpenCode 会话原始 JSON 导出到 `logs/trace/llm_chat_log.json`，不得删改、摘要或使用脱敏导出替代原记录。
135: - `logs/trace/trace-manifest.json` 必须记录会话 ID、OpenCode 版本、消息数量、会话文件哈希、C/Rust 哈希和验证产物索引。
136: - 构建、C 链接、双向兼容、覆盖率、API 和安全门禁的 JSON 与原始输出日志必须同步到 `logs/trace/verification/`。
137: - 最终判断必须重新检查源码、静态库、C/Rust 运行行为和持久化字节，不得采信会话文本中的“完成”“通过”或代理自评。
138: 
139: ## VER-01 完成必须有独立证据
140: 
141: - 每个行为切片必须依次经过：C 证据、先失败的 Rust 验收测试、最小实现、聚焦测试、全量测试。
142: - 最终必须同时通过 Rust 构建、Rust 测试、原 C 测试链接运行、C case 覆盖、模块覆盖、规范合规、安全审计和占位审计。
143: - `reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv` 的每条规范必须为 `PASS` 并写出可定位到文件、测试、命令或运行轨迹的证据。
144: - 报告中的 `PASS` 不是证据本身；无法指出具体产物或结果时必须保持 `PENDING` 并继续工作。
145: 
146: ## 强制产物格式
147: 
148: `reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv`：
149: 
150: ```text
151: rule_id\tstatus\tevidence
152: BASE-01\tPASS\treports/evidence/final-source.json
153: ```
154: 
155: `reports/c-module-coverage.tsv`：
156: 
157: ```text
158: c_file\tc_symbols\trust_files\trust_tests\tevidence\tstatus
159: src/fdb_utils.c\tfdb_calc_crc32;_fdb_set_status\tsrc/layout.rs;src/crc.rs\tlayout_matches_c_probe;crc_matches_c_trace\treports/evidence/final-interop.json\tPASS
160: ```
161: 
162: `reports/c-test-coverage.tsv` 的 `evidence` 必须指向运行准确 Rust 测试名的结构化 JSON；
163: `reports/c-api-coverage.tsv` 的 `evidence` 必须指向 C 链接或双向兼容门禁 JSON。
164: 多个值使用分号分隔。证据必须具体且可复查，不得写 `N/A`、`TODO`、`TBD`、`skip`、“待完成”或泛化描述。

- 原 C 测试使用到的公开符号必须由 release 静态库导出，并能由原头文件声明直接编译和链接。
- FFI 函数必须使用 `extern "C"`、稳定符号名和与 C 声明一致的参数/返回类型；需要时使用 `#[repr(C)]`。
- 指针的空值、长度、生命周期、别名和可写性必须在边界检查，内部立即转换为安全 Rust 表达。
- Rust panic 不得跨越 FFI 边界；边界必须转换为 C 能识别的错误码或失败结果。
- C 分配/C 释放、Rust 分配/Rust 释放不得交叉错配。

## MEM-01 默认使用安全 Rust

- 所有权数据使用 `Vec<u8>` 或固定数组，借用数据使用切片，可空语义使用 `Option`，错误使用 `Result`。
- 每次地址加法、长度相加、切片范围和指针转切片都必须先检查溢出与边界。
- 禁止 `static mut`；共享可变状态必须使用锁、原子类型或线程局部状态，并保持 C 的生命周期语义。
- `unsafe` 只能位于不可避免的 FFI 或底层边界，范围必须最小，并在附近写明安全前提。
- 禁止在生产代码中使用 `unwrap()`、`expect()`、`todo!()`、`unimplemented!()` 或占位实现。

## ERR-01 错误和输出参数语义必须保留

- 必须建立 C 错误码与 Rust 错误类型的完整映射，保留成功、未找到、无空间、读取失败、写入失败、校验失败等差异。
- C 输出参数只有在源实现会写入时才可修改；失败时是否保留旧值必须以 C 行为为准。
- 内部可以把输出参数改为 `Result<T, FdbErr>` 或 `Option<T>`，但 FFI 边界必须还原 C 调用约定。
- 禁止吞掉后端错误、用默认值代替错误或把不同错误统一成成功/未找到。

## CBK-01 回调和控制参数必须类型化且保持调用契约

- flash 回调应在安全核心中建模为 trait 方法，`void *` 控制参数应转换为有类型的枚举或结构。
- 必须保留回调调用次数、顺序、停止条件、用户上下文和回调返回值对控制流的影响。
- FFI 回调保存时间不得超过 C 生命周期保证；禁止长期持有未经证明有效的裸指针。
- 可选回调和空上下文必须显式建模，不能用伪地址或全局可变变量替代。

## GLB-01 全局状态、重入和并发边界必须明确

- 必须盘点 C 全局/静态状态，区分库状态、数据库实例状态和测试计数器。
- 实例状态必须归属对应 Rust 对象；测试计数器可使用 `thread_local!` 与 `Cell`，不得污染其他测试。
- 若 C 实现不保证线程安全，Rust 不得虚假宣称线程安全；若暴露 `Send`/`Sync`，必须有类型与同步证据。
- 初始化、反初始化、重复初始化和多实例互不干扰必须有测试。

## EVD-01 证据必须绑定当前输入和当前实现

- 成功证据必须由固定运行器生成 JSON 和日志，记录命令、退出码、时间、日志哈希、C 输入哈希和 Rust 目标哈希。
- 修改 `Cargo.toml`、`src/` 或 `tests/` 后，此前证据全部失效，必须冻结实现后重新运行。
- C case 行必须绑定包含准确 Rust 测试名的聚焦 `cargo test` 命令；API、模块和规范行必须绑定对应门禁命令。
- 禁止手写证据 JSON、复用失败日志、引用不存在的路径，或用自然语言 `PASS` 代替可校验证据。

## LOG-01 AI 交互和验证日志必须完整留存

- 必须把当前项目的完整 OpenCode 会话原始 JSON 导出到 `logs/trace/llm_chat_log.json`，不得删改、摘要或使用脱敏导出替代原记录。
- `logs/trace/trace-manifest.json` 必须记录会话 ID、OpenCode 版本、消息数量、会话文件哈希、C/Rust 哈希和验证产物索引。
- 构建、C 链接、双向兼容、覆盖率、API 和安全门禁的 JSON 与原始输出日志必须同步到 `logs/trace/verification/`。
- 最终判断必须重新检查源码、静态库、C/Rust 运行行为和持久化字节，不得采信会话文本中的“完成”“通过”或代理自评。

## VER-01 完成必须有独立证据

- 每个行为切片必须依次经过：C 证据、先失败的 Rust 验收测试、最小实现、聚焦测试、全量测试。
- 最终必须同时通过 Rust 构建、Rust 测试、原 C 测试链接运行、C case 覆盖、模块覆盖、规范合规、安全审计和占位审计。
- `reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv` 的每条规范必须为 `PASS` 并写出可定位到文件、测试、命令或运行轨迹的证据。
- 报告中的 `PASS` 不是证据本身；无法指出具体产物或结果时必须保持 `PENDING` 并继续工作。

## 强制产物格式

`reports/c-to-rust-compliance.tsv`：

```text
rule_id\tstatus\tevidence
BASE-01\tPASS\treports/evidence/final-source.json
```

`reports/c-module-coverage.tsv`：

```text
c_file\tc_symbols\trust_files\trust_tests\tevidence\tstatus
src/fdb_utils.c\tfdb_calc_crc32;_fdb_set_status\tsrc/layout.rs;src/crc.rs\tlayout_matches_c_probe;crc_matches_c_trace\treports/evidence/final-interop.json\tPASS
```

`reports/c-test-coverage.tsv` 的 `evidence` 必须指向运行准确 Rust 测试名的结构化 JSON；
`reports/c-api-coverage.tsv` 的 `evidence` 必须指向 C 链接或双向兼容门禁 JSON。
多个值使用分号分隔。证据必须具体且可复查，不得写 `N/A`、`TODO`、`TBD`、`skip`、“待完成”或泛化描述。

> **Note**: This project is forked from [armink/FlashDB](https://gitee.com/armink/FlashDB) for practicing high-performance programming. Non-Linux platform code (STM32, ESP32/8266, Zephyr demos and ports) has been removed, and Linux unit tests and performance benchmarks have been added.

## Introduction

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) is a lightweight Flash database that focuses on providing data storage solutions for IoT and embedded products. Different from traditional database based on file system, [FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) combines the features of Flash and has strong performance and reliability. And under the premise of ensuring extremely low resource occupation, the service life of Flash should be extended as much as possible.

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) provides two database modes:

- **Key-value database**: It is a non-relational database that stores data as a collection of key-value pairs, where the key is used as a unique identifier. KVDB has simple operation and strong scalability.
- **Time Series Database**: Time Series Database (TSDB), which stores data in **time sequence**. TSDB data has a timestamp, a large amount of data storage, and high insertion and query performance.

## Usage scenario

FlashDB provides a variety of data storage solutions, not only has a small resource footprint, but also has a large storage capacity, which is very suitable for IoT products. The following are the main application scenarios:

- **Key-value database**:
  - Product parameter storage
  - User configuration information storage
  - Small file management
- **Time Series Database**: 
  - Store dynamically generated structured data: such as environmental monitoring information collected by temperature and humidity sensors, human health information recorded in real time by smart bracelets, etc.
  - Record operation log: store operation log of product history, record of abnormal alarm, etc.

## Key Features

- Very small footprint, ram usage is almost **0**;
- Support multiple partitions, **multiple instances**. When the amount of data is large, the partition can be refined to reduce the retrieval time;
- Support **wear balance** to extend Flash life;
- Support **Power-off protection** function, high reliability;
- Supports two KV types, string and blob, which is convenient for users to operate;
- Support KV **incremental upgrade**, after product firmware upgrade, KVDB content also supports automatic upgrade;
- Support to modify the status of each TSDB record to facilitate user management;
- Support POSIX file mode for Linux and other POSIX platforms;

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Path             | Storage Type |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------ |
| linux    | `demos/linux`    | posix file   |

## How to use

FlashDB provides comprehensive documentation, see: https://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/

Quick access:

- [Quick Start Document](http://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/quick-started)
- [Porting Document](http://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/porting)
- [Configuration Document](http://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/configuration)
- [API Document](http://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/api)

## License

The project uses the Apache-2.0 open source protocol. For details, please read the contents of the LICENSE file in the project.

77: uint32_t fdb_calc_crc32(uint32_t crc, const void *buf, size_t size)
78: {
79:     const uint8_t *p;
80: 
81:     p = (const uint8_t *)buf;
82:     crc = crc ^ ~0U;
83: 
84:     while (size--) {
85:         crc = crc32_table[(crc ^ *p++) & 0xFF] ^ (crc >> 8);
86:     }
87: 
88:     return crc ^ ~0U;

92: {

94:     /*
95:      * | write garn |       status0       |       status1       |      status2         |       status3      |
96:      * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
97:      * |    1bit    | 0xFF                | 0x7F                |  0x3F                |  0x1F
98:      * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
99:      * |    8bit    | 0xFF FF FF          | 0x00 FF FF          |  0x00 00 FF          |  0x00 00 00
100:      * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
101:      * |   32bit    | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF | 0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF 00FFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF 00FFFFFF
102:      * |            | 0xFFFFFFFF          | 0xFFFFFFFF          |  0xFFFFFFFF          |  0x00FFFFFF
103:      * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
104:      * |            | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF | 0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF
105:      * |   64bit    | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF
106:      * |            | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF | 0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0xFFFFFFFF FFFFFFFF |  0x00FFFFFF FFFFFFFF
107:      */
108:     memset(status_table, FDB_BYTE_ERASED, FDB_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE(status_num));
109:     if (status_index > 0) {
110: #if (FDB_WRITE_GRAN == 1)
111:         byte_index = (status_index - 1) / 8;
112: #if (FDB_BYTE_ERASED == 0xFF)
113:         status_table[byte_index] &= (0x00ff >> (status_index % 8));
114: #else
115:         status_table[byte_index] |= (0x00ff >> (status_index % 8));
116: #endif
117: #else
118:         byte_index = (status_index - 1) * (FDB_WRITE_GRAN / 8);
119:         status_table[byte_index] = FDB_BYTE_WRITTEN;
120: #endif /* FDB_WRITE_GRAN == 1 */
121:     }

133:         if ((status_table[status_num / 8] & (0x80 >> (status_num % 8))) == 0x00) {

137:         if (status_table[status_num * FDB_WRITE_GRAN / 8] == FDB_BYTE_WRITTEN) {

159:                 memcpy(&db->sector_cache_table[i], sector, sizeof(struct kvdb_sec_info));
160:             } else {
161:                 db->sector_cache_table[i].addr = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
162:             }
163:             return;
164:         } else if (db->sector_cache_table[i].addr == FDB_DATA_UNUSED) {
165:             empty_index = i;
166:         }
167:     }
168:     /* add the sector empty_addr to cache */
169:     if (sector->check_ok && empty_index < FDB_SECTOR_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE) {
170:         memcpy(&db->sector_cache_table[empty_index], sector, sizeof(struct kvdb_sec_info));
171:     }
172: }

207: static void update_kv_cache(fdb_kvdb_t db, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint32_t addr)
208: {
209:     size_t i, empty_index = FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE, min_activity_index = FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE;
210:     uint16_t name_crc = (uint16_t) (fdb_calc_crc32(0, name, name_len) >> 16), min_activity = 0xFFFF;
211: 
212:     for (i = 0; i < FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE; i++) {
213:         if (addr != FDB_DATA_UNUSED) {
214:             /* update the KV address in cache */
215:             if (db->kv_cache_table[i].name_crc == name_crc) {
216:                 db->kv_cache_table[i].addr = addr;
217:                 return;
218:             } else if ((db->kv_cache_table[i].addr == FDB_DATA_UNUSED) && (empty_index == FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE)) {
219:                 empty_index = i;
220:             } else if (db->kv_cache_table[i].addr != FDB_DATA_UNUSED) {
221:                 if (db->kv_cache_table[i].active > 0) {
222:                     db->kv_cache_table[i].active--;
223:                 }
224:                 if (db->kv_cache_table[i].active < min_activity) {
225:                     min_activity_index = i;
226:                     min_activity = db->kv_cache_table[i].active;
227:                 }
228:             }
229:         } else if (db->kv_cache_table[i].name_crc == name_crc) {
230:             /* delete the KV */
231:             db->kv_cache_table[i].addr = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
232:             db->kv_cache_table[i].active = 0;
233:             return;
234:         }
235:     }
236:     /* add the KV to cache, using LRU (Least Recently Used) like algorithm */
237:     if (empty_index < FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE) {
238:         db->kv_cache_table[empty_index].addr = addr;
239:         db->kv_cache_table[empty_index].name_crc = name_crc;
240:         db->kv_cache_table[empty_index].active = FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE;
241:     } else if (min_activity_index < FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE) {
242:         db->kv_cache_table[min_activity_index].addr = addr;
243:         db->kv_cache_table[min_activity_index].name_crc = name_crc;
244:         db->kv_cache_table[min_activity_index].active = FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE;
245:     }
246: }

248: /*
249:  * Get KV info from cache. It's return true when cache is hit.
250:  */
251: static bool get_kv_from_cache(fdb_kvdb_t db, const char *name, size_t name_len, uint32_t *addr)
252: {
253:     size_t i;
254:     uint16_t name_crc = (uint16_t) (fdb_calc_crc32(0, name, name_len) >> 16);
255: 
256:     for (i = 0; i < FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE; i++) {
257:         if ((db->kv_cache_table[i].addr != FDB_DATA_UNUSED) && (db->kv_cache_table[i].name_crc == name_crc)) {
258:             char saved_name[FDB_KV_NAME_MAX] = { 0 };
259:             /* read the KV name in flash */
260:             _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, db->kv_cache_table[i].addr + KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE, (uint32_t *) saved_name, FDB_KV_NAME_MAX);
261:             if (!strncmp(name, saved_name, name_len)) {
262:                 *addr = db->kv_cache_table[i].addr;
263:                 if (db->kv_cache_table[i].active >= 0xFFFF - FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE) {
264:                     db->kv_cache_table[i].active = 0xFFFF;
265:                 } else {
266:                     db->kv_cache_table[i].active += FDB_KV_CACHE_TABLE_SIZE;
267:                 }
268:                 return true;
269:             }
270:         }
271:     }
272: 
273:     return false;
274: }
275: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */

277: /*
278:  * find the next KV address by magic word on the flash
279:  */
280: static uint32_t find_next_kv_addr(fdb_kvdb_t db, uint32_t start, uint32_t end)
281: {
282:     uint8_t buf[32];
283:     uint32_t start_bak = start, i;
284:     uint32_t magic;
285: 
286: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
287:     kv_sec_info_t sector;
288:     sector = get_sector_from_cache(db, FDB_ALIGN_DOWN(start, db_sec_size(db)));
289:     if (sector && start == sector->empty_kv) {
290:         return FAILED_ADDR;
291:     }
292: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
293: 
294:     for (; start < end && start + sizeof(buf) < end; start += (sizeof(buf) - sizeof(uint32_t))) {
295:         if (_fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, start, (uint32_t *) buf, sizeof(buf)) != FDB_NO_ERR)
296:             return FAILED_ADDR;
297:         for (i = 0; i < sizeof(buf) - sizeof(uint32_t) && start + i < end; i++) {
298: #ifndef FDB_BIG_ENDIAN            /* Little Endian Order */
299:             magic = buf[i] + ((uint32_t)buf[i + 1] << 8) + ((uint32_t)buf[i + 2] << 16) + ((uint32_t)buf[i + 3] << 24);
300: #else                       /* Big Endian Order */
301:             magic = buf[i + 3] + ((uint32_t)buf[i + 2] << 8) + ((uint32_t)buf[i + 1] << 16) + ((uint32_t)buf[i] << 24);
302: #endif
303:             if (magic == KV_MAGIC_WORD && (start + i - KV_MAGIC_OFFSET) >= start_bak) {
304:                 return start + i - KV_MAGIC_OFFSET;
305:             }
306:         }
307:     }
308: 
309:     return FAILED_ADDR;
310: }

312: static uint32_t get_next_kv_addr(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, fdb_kv_t pre_kv)
313: {
314:     uint32_t addr = FAILED_ADDR;
315: 
316:     if (sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY) {
317:         return FAILED_ADDR;
318:     }
319: 
320:     if (pre_kv->addr.start == FAILED_ADDR) {
321:         /* the first KV address */
322:         addr = sector->addr + SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
323:     } else {
324:         if (pre_kv->addr.start <= sector->addr + db_sec_size(db)) {
325:             if (pre_kv->crc_is_ok) {
326:                 addr = pre_kv->addr.start + pre_kv->len;
327:             } else {
328:                 /* when pre_kv CRC check failed, maybe the flash has error data
329:                  * find_next_kv_addr after pre_kv address */
330:                 addr = pre_kv->addr.start + FDB_WG_ALIGN(1);
331:             }
332:             /* check and find next KV address */
333:             addr = find_next_kv_addr(db, addr, sector->addr + db_sec_size(db) - SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE);
334: 
335:             if (addr == FAILED_ADDR || addr > sector->addr + db_sec_size(db) || pre_kv->len == 0) {
336:                 //TODO Sector continuous mode
337:                 return FAILED_ADDR;
338:             }
339:         } else {
340:             /* no KV */
341:             return FAILED_ADDR;
342:         }
343:     }
344: 
345:     return addr;
346: }

348: static fdb_err_t read_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, fdb_kv_t kv)
349: {
350:     struct kv_hdr_data kv_hdr;
351:     uint8_t buf[32];
352:     uint32_t calc_crc32 = 0, crc_data_len, kv_name_addr;
353:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
354:     size_t len, size;
355:     /* read KV header raw data */
356:     _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, kv->addr.start, (uint32_t *)&kv_hdr, sizeof(struct kv_hdr_data));
357:     kv->status = (fdb_kv_status_t) _fdb_get_status(kv_hdr.status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM);
358:     kv->len = kv_hdr.len;
359: 
360:     if (kv->len == UINT32_MAX || kv->len > db_max_size(db) || kv->len < KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE) {
361:         /* the KV length was not write, so reserved the info for current KV */
362:         kv->len = KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
363:         if (kv->status != FDB_KV_ERR_HDR) {
364:             kv->status = FDB_KV_ERR_HDR;
365:             FDB_INFO("Error: The KV @0x%08" PRIX32 " length has an error.\n", kv->addr.start);
366:             _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, kv->addr.start, kv_hdr.status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_ERR_HDR, true);
367:         }
368:         kv->crc_is_ok = false;
369:         return FDB_READ_ERR;
370:     } else if (kv->len > db_sec_size(db) - SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE && kv->len < db_max_size(db)) {
371:         //TODO Sector continuous mode, or the write length is not written completely
372:     }
373: 
374:     /* CRC32 data len(header.name_len + header.value_len + name + value), using sizeof(uint32_t) for compatible V1.x */
375:     calc_crc32 = fdb_calc_crc32(calc_crc32, &kv_hdr.name_len, sizeof(uint32_t));
376:     calc_crc32 = fdb_calc_crc32(calc_crc32, &kv_hdr.value_len, sizeof(uint32_t));
377:     crc_data_len = kv->len - KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
378:     /* calculate the CRC32 value */
379:     for (len = 0, size = 0; len < crc_data_len; len += size) {
380:         if (len + sizeof(buf) < crc_data_len) {
381:             size = sizeof(buf);
382:         } else {
383:             size = crc_data_len - len;
384:         }
385: 
386:         _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, kv->addr.start + KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE + len, (uint32_t *) buf, FDB_WG_ALIGN(size));
387:         calc_crc32 = fdb_calc_crc32(calc_crc32, buf, size);
388:     }
389:     /* check CRC32 */
390:     if (calc_crc32 != kv_hdr.crc32) {
391:         size_t name_len = kv_hdr.name_len > FDB_KV_NAME_MAX ? FDB_KV_NAME_MAX : kv_hdr.name_len;
392:         kv->crc_is_ok = false;
393:         result = FDB_READ_ERR;
394:         /* try read the KV name, maybe read name has error */
395:         kv_name_addr = kv->addr.start + KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
396:         _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, kv_name_addr, (uint32_t *)kv->name, FDB_WG_ALIGN(name_len));
397:         FDB_INFO("Error: Read the KV (%.*s@0x%08" PRIX32 ") CRC32 check failed!\n", name_len, kv->name, kv->addr.start);
398:     } else {
399:         kv->crc_is_ok = true;
400:         /* the name is behind aligned KV header */
401:         kv_name_addr = kv->addr.start + KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
402:         _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, kv_name_addr, (uint32_t *) kv->name, FDB_WG_ALIGN(kv_hdr.name_len));
403:         /* the value is behind aligned name */
404:         kv->addr.value = kv_name_addr + FDB_WG_ALIGN(kv_hdr.name_len);
405:         kv->value_len = kv_hdr.value_len;
406:         kv->name_len = kv_hdr.name_len;
407:         if (kv_hdr.name_len >= sizeof(kv->name) / sizeof(kv->name[0])) {
408:             kv_hdr.name_len = sizeof(kv->name) / sizeof(kv->name[0]) - 1;
409:         }
410:         kv->name[kv_hdr.name_len] = '\0';
411:     }
412: 
413:     return result;
414: }

416: static fdb_err_t read_sector_info(fdb_kvdb_t db, uint32_t addr, kv_sec_info_t sector, bool traversal)
417: {
418:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
419:     struct sector_hdr_data sec_hdr = { 0 };
420: 
421:     FDB_ASSERT(addr % db_sec_size(db) == 0);
422:     FDB_ASSERT(sector);
423: 
424: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
425:     kv_sec_info_t sector_cache = get_sector_from_cache(db, addr);
426:     if (sector_cache && ((!traversal) || (traversal && sector_cache->empty_kv != FAILED_ADDR))) {
427:         memcpy(sector, sector_cache, sizeof(struct kvdb_sec_info));
428:         return result;
429:     }
430: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
431: 
432:     /* read sector header raw data */
433:     _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, addr, (uint32_t *)&sec_hdr, sizeof(struct sector_hdr_data));
434: 
435:     sector->status.store = FDB_SECTOR_STORE_UNUSED;
436:     sector->status.dirty = FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_UNUSED;
437:     sector->addr = addr;
438:     sector->magic = sec_hdr.magic;
439:     /* check magic word and combined value */
440:     if (sector->magic != SECTOR_MAGIC_WORD ||
441:         (sec_hdr.combined != SECTOR_NOT_COMBINED && sec_hdr.combined != SECTOR_COMBINED)) {
442:         sector->check_ok = false;
443:         sector->combined = SECTOR_NOT_COMBINED;
444:         return FDB_INIT_FAILED;
445:     }
446:     sector->check_ok = true;
447:     /* get other sector info */
448:     sector->combined = sec_hdr.combined;
449:     sector->status.store = (fdb_sector_store_status_t) _fdb_get_status(sec_hdr.status_table.store, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM);
450:     sector->status.dirty = (fdb_sector_dirty_status_t) _fdb_get_status(sec_hdr.status_table.dirty, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_STATUS_NUM);
451:     /* traversal all KV and calculate the remain space size */
452:     if (traversal) {
453:         sector->remain = 0;
454:         sector->empty_kv = sector->addr + SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
455:         if (sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY) {
456:             sector->remain = db_sec_size(db) - SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
457:         }
458:         else if (sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING) {
459:             struct fdb_kv kv_obj;
460: 
461:             sector->remain = db_sec_size(db) - SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
462:             kv_obj.addr.start = sector->addr + SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
463:             do {
464:                 read_kv(db, &kv_obj);
465:                 if (!kv_obj.crc_is_ok) {
466:                     if (kv_obj.status != FDB_KV_PRE_WRITE && kv_obj.status != FDB_KV_ERR_HDR) {
467:                         sector->remain = 0;
468:                         result = FDB_READ_ERR;
469:                         break;
470:                     }
471:                 }
472:                 sector->empty_kv += kv_obj.len;
473:                 sector->remain -= kv_obj.len;
474:             } while ((kv_obj.addr.start = get_next_kv_addr(db, sector, &kv_obj)) != FAILED_ADDR);
475:             /* check the empty KV address by read continue 0xFF on flash  */
476:             {
477:                 uint32_t ff_addr;
478: 
479:                 ff_addr = _fdb_continue_ff_addr((fdb_db_t)db, sector->empty_kv, sector->addr + db_sec_size(db));
480:                 /* check the flash data is clean */
481:                 if (sector->empty_kv != ff_addr) {
482:                     /* update the sector information */
483:                     sector->empty_kv = ff_addr;
484:                     sector->remain = db_sec_size(db) - (ff_addr - sector->addr);
485:                 }
486:             }
487: 
488:         }
489: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
490:         update_sector_cache(db, sector);
491:     } else {
492:         kv_sec_info_t sec_cache = get_sector_from_cache(db, sector->addr);
493:         if (!sec_cache) {
494:             sector->empty_kv = FAILED_ADDR;
495:             sector->remain = 0;
496:             update_sector_cache(db, sector);
497:         }
498: #endif
499:     }
500: 
501:     return result;
502: }
503: 
504: static uint32_t get_next_sector_addr(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t pre_sec, uint32_t traversed_len)
505: {
506:     uint32_t cur_block_size;
507: 
508:     if (pre_sec->combined == SECTOR_NOT_COMBINED) {
509:         cur_block_size = db_sec_size(db);
510:     } else {
511:         cur_block_size = pre_sec->combined * db_sec_size(db);
512:     }
513: 
514:     if (traversed_len + cur_block_size <= db_max_size(db)) {
515:         /* if reach to the end, roll back to the first sector */
516:         if (pre_sec->addr + cur_block_size < db_max_size(db)) {
517:             return pre_sec->addr + cur_block_size;
518:         } else {
519:             /* the next sector is on the top of the database */
520:             return 0;
521:         }
522:     } else {
523:         /* finished */
524:         return FAILED_ADDR;
525:     }
526: }

528: static void kv_iterator(fdb_kvdb_t db, fdb_kv_t kv, void *arg1, void *arg2,
529:         bool (*callback)(fdb_kv_t kv, void *arg1, void *arg2))
530: {
531:     struct kvdb_sec_info sector;
532:     uint32_t sec_addr, traversed_len = 0;
533: 
534:     sec_addr = db_oldest_addr(db);
535:     /* search all sectors */
536:     do {
537:         traversed_len += db_sec_size(db);
538:         if (read_sector_info(db, sec_addr, &sector, false) != FDB_NO_ERR) {
539:             continue;
540:         }
541:         if (callback == NULL) {
542:             continue;
543:         }
544:         /* sector has KV */
545:         if (sector.status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING || sector.status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_FULL) {
546:             kv->addr.start = sector.addr + SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE;
547:             /* search all KV */
548:             do {
549:                 read_kv(db, kv);
550:                 /* iterator is interrupted when callback return true */
551:                 if (callback(kv, arg1, arg2)) {
552:                     return;
553:                 }
554:             } while ((kv->addr.start = get_next_kv_addr(db, &sector, kv)) != FAILED_ADDR);
555:         }
556:     } while ((sec_addr = get_next_sector_addr(db, &sector, traversed_len)) != FAILED_ADDR);
557: }

559: static bool find_kv_cb(fdb_kv_t kv, void *arg1, void *arg2)

564: 
565:     if (key_len != kv->name_len) {
566:         return false;
567:     }
568:     /* check KV */
569:     if (kv->crc_is_ok && kv->status == FDB_KV_WRITE && !strncmp(kv->name, key, key_len)) {
570:         *find_ok = true;
571:         return true;
572:     }
573:     return false;
574: }

585: static bool find_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, const char *key, fdb_kv_t kv)
586: {
587:     bool find_ok = false;
588: 
589: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
590:     size_t key_len = strlen(key);
591: 
592:     if (get_kv_from_cache(db, key, key_len, &kv->addr.start)) {
593:         read_kv(db, kv);
594:         return true;
595:     }
596: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
597: 
598:     find_ok = find_kv_no_cache(db, key, kv);
599: 
600: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
601:     if (find_ok) {
602:         update_kv_cache(db, key, key_len, kv->addr.start);
603:     }
604: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
605: 
606:     return find_ok;
607: }

646: /**
647:  * Get a KV object by key name
648:  *
649:  * @param db database object
650:  * @param key KV name
651:  * @param kv KV object
652:  *
653:  * @return KV object when is not NULL
654:  */
655: fdb_kv_t fdb_kv_get_obj(fdb_kvdb_t db, const char *key, fdb_kv_t kv)
656: {

755: static fdb_err_t write_kv_hdr(fdb_kvdb_t db, uint32_t addr, kv_hdr_data_t kv_hdr)
756: {
757:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
758:     /* write the status will by write granularity */
759:     result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, addr, kv_hdr->status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_PRE_WRITE, false);
760:     if (result != FDB_NO_ERR) {
761:         return result;
762:     }
763:     /* write other header data */
764:     result = _fdb_flash_write((fdb_db_t)db, addr + KV_MAGIC_OFFSET, &kv_hdr->magic, sizeof(struct kv_hdr_data) - KV_MAGIC_OFFSET, false);
765: 
766:     return result;
767: }

769: static fdb_err_t format_sector(fdb_kvdb_t db, uint32_t addr, uint32_t combined_value)
770: {
771:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
772:     struct sector_hdr_data sec_hdr = { 0 };
773: 
774:     FDB_ASSERT(addr % db_sec_size(db) == 0);
775: 
776:     result = _fdb_flash_erase((fdb_db_t)db, addr, db_sec_size(db));
777:     if (result == FDB_NO_ERR) {
778:         /* initialize the header data */
779:         memset(&sec_hdr, FDB_BYTE_ERASED, sizeof(struct sector_hdr_data));
780: #if (FDB_WRITE_GRAN == 1)
781:         _fdb_set_status(sec_hdr.status_table.store, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY);
782:         _fdb_set_status(sec_hdr.status_table.dirty, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_STATUS_NUM, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_FALSE);
783:         sec_hdr.magic = SECTOR_MAGIC_WORD;
784:         sec_hdr.combined = combined_value;
785:         sec_hdr.reserved = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
786:         /* save the header */
787:         result = _fdb_flash_write((fdb_db_t)db, addr, (uint32_t *)&sec_hdr, SECTOR_HDR_DATA_SIZE, true);
788: #else   // separate the whole "sec_hdr" program to several single program operations to prevent re-program issue on
789:         // flash that does not support repeated write
790:         /* write the sector store status */
791:         _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db,
792:                           addr + SECTOR_STORE_OFFSET,
793:                           sec_hdr.status_table.store,
794:                           FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM,
795:                           FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY,
796:                           true);
797: 
798:         /* write the sector dirty status */
799:         _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db,
800:                           addr + SECTOR_DIRTY_OFFSET,
801:                           sec_hdr.status_table.dirty,
802:                           FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_STATUS_NUM,
803:                           FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_FALSE,
804:                           true);
805: 
806:         /* write the magic word and combined next sector number */
807:         sec_hdr.magic = SECTOR_MAGIC_WORD;
808:         sec_hdr.combined = combined_value;
809:         sec_hdr.reserved = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
810:         result = _fdb_flash_write((fdb_db_t)db,
811:                                   addr + SECTOR_MAGIC_OFFSET,
812:                                   (void *)(&(sec_hdr.magic)),
813:                                   (sizeof(struct sector_hdr_data) - SECTOR_MAGIC_OFFSET),
814:                                   true);
815: #endif
816: 
817: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
818:         {
819:             struct kvdb_sec_info sector = {.addr = addr, .check_ok = false, .empty_kv = FAILED_ADDR };
820:             /* delete the sector cache */
821:             update_sector_cache(db, &sector);
822:         }
823: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
824:     }
825: 
826:     return result;
827: }
828: 
829: static fdb_err_t update_sec_status(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, size_t new_kv_len, bool *is_full)
830: {
831:     uint8_t status_table[FDB_STORE_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
832:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
833:     /* change the current sector status */
834:     if (sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY) {
835:         /* change the sector status to using */
836:         result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, sector->addr, status_table, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING, true);
837: 
838: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
839:         update_sector_status_store_cache(db, sector->addr, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING);
840: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
841: 
842:     } else if (sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING) {
843:         /* check remain size */
844:         if (sector->remain < FDB_SEC_REMAIN_THRESHOLD || sector->remain - new_kv_len < FDB_SEC_REMAIN_THRESHOLD) {
845:             /* change the sector status to full */
846:             result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, sector->addr, status_table, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_FULL, true);
847: 
848: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
849:             update_sector_status_store_cache(db, sector->addr, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_FULL);
850: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
851: 
852:             if (is_full) {
853:                 *is_full = true;
854:             }
855:         } else if (is_full) {
856:             *is_full = false;
857:         }
858:     }
859: 
860:     return result;
861: }
862: 
863: static void sector_iterator(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, fdb_sector_store_status_t status, void *arg1, void *arg2,
864:         bool (*callback)(kv_sec_info_t sector, void *arg1, void *arg2), bool traversal_kv)
865: {
866:     uint32_t sec_addr, traversed_len = 0;
867: 
868:     /* search all sectors */
869:     sec_addr = db_oldest_addr(db);
870:     do {
871:         traversed_len += db_sec_size(db);
872:         read_sector_info(db, sec_addr, sector, false);
873:         if (status == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_UNUSED || status == sector->status.store) {
874:             if (traversal_kv) {
875:                 read_sector_info(db, sec_addr, sector, true);
876:             }
877:             /* iterator is interrupted when callback return true */
878:             if (callback && callback(sector, arg1, arg2)) {
879:                 return;
880:             }
881:         }
882:     } while ((sec_addr = get_next_sector_addr(db, sector, traversed_len)) != FAILED_ADDR);
883: }

885: static bool sector_statistics_cb(kv_sec_info_t sector, void *arg1, void *arg2)
886: {
887:     size_t *empty_sector = arg1, *using_sector = arg2;
888: 
889:     if (sector->check_ok && sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY) {
890:         (*empty_sector)++;
891:     } else if (sector->check_ok && sector->status.store == FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING) {
892:         (*using_sector)++;
893:     }
894: 
895:     return false;
896: }

898: static bool alloc_kv_cb(kv_sec_info_t sector, void *arg1, void *arg2)
899: {
900:     struct alloc_kv_cb_args *arg = arg1;
901: 
902:     /* 1. sector has space
903:      * 2. the NO dirty sector
904:      * 3. the dirty sector only when the gc_request is false */
905:     if (sector->check_ok && sector->remain > arg->kv_size + FDB_SEC_REMAIN_THRESHOLD
906:             && ((sector->status.dirty == FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_FALSE)
907:                     || (sector->status.dirty == FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_TRUE && !arg->db->gc_request))) {
908:         *(arg->empty_kv) = sector->empty_kv;
909:         return true;
910:     }
911: 
912:     return false;
913: }
914: 
915: static uint32_t alloc_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, size_t kv_size)
916: {
917:     uint32_t empty_kv = FAILED_ADDR;
918:     size_t empty_sector = 0, using_sector = 0;
919:     struct alloc_kv_cb_args arg = {db, kv_size, &empty_kv};
920: 
921:     /* sector status statistics */
922:     sector_iterator(db, sector, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_UNUSED, &empty_sector, &using_sector, sector_statistics_cb, false);
923:     if (using_sector > 0) {
924:         /* alloc the KV from the using status sector first */
925:         sector_iterator(db, sector, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_USING, &arg, NULL, alloc_kv_cb, true);
926:     }
927:     if (empty_sector > 0 && empty_kv == FAILED_ADDR) {
928:         if (empty_sector > FDB_GC_EMPTY_SEC_THRESHOLD || db->gc_request) {
929:             sector_iterator(db, sector, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_EMPTY, &arg, NULL, alloc_kv_cb, true);
930:         } else {
931:             /* no space for new KV now will GC and retry */
932:             FDB_DEBUG("Trigger a GC check after alloc KV failed.\n");
933:             db->gc_request = true;
934:         }
935:     }
936: 
937:     return empty_kv;
938: }

940: static fdb_err_t del_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, const char *key, fdb_kv_t old_kv, bool complete_del)
941: {
942:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
943:     uint32_t dirty_status_addr;
944:     struct fdb_kv kv = { .status = FDB_KV_UNUSED };
945: 
946: #if (KV_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE >= FDB_DIRTY_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE)
947:     uint8_t status_table[KV_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
948: #else
949:     uint8_t status_table[DIRTY_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
950: #endif
951: 
952:     /* need find KV */
953:     if (!old_kv) {
954:         /* find KV */
955:         if (find_kv(db, key, &kv)) {
956:             old_kv = &kv;
957:         } else {
958:             FDB_DEBUG("Not found '%s' in KV.\n", key);
959:             return FDB_KV_NAME_ERR;
960:         }
961:     }
962:     /* change and save the new status */
963:     if (!complete_del) {
964:         result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, old_kv->addr.start, status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_PRE_DELETE, false);
965:         db->last_is_complete_del = true;
966:     } else {
967:         result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, old_kv->addr.start, status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_DELETED, true);
968: 
969:         if (!db->last_is_complete_del && result == FDB_NO_ERR) {
970: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
971:             /* delete the KV in flash and cache */
972:             if (key != NULL) {
973:                 /* when using del_kv(db, key, NULL, true) or del_kv(db, key, kv, true) in fdb_del_kv(db, ) and set_kv(db, ) */
974:                 update_kv_cache(db, key, strlen(key), FDB_DATA_UNUSED);
975:             } else if (old_kv != NULL) {
976:                 /* when using del_kv(db, NULL, kv, true) in move_kv(db, ) */
977:                 update_kv_cache(db, old_kv->name, old_kv->name_len, FDB_DATA_UNUSED);
978:             }
979: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
980:         }
981: 
982:         db->last_is_complete_del = false;
983:     }
984: 
985:     dirty_status_addr = FDB_ALIGN_DOWN(old_kv->addr.start, db_sec_size(db)) + SECTOR_DIRTY_OFFSET;
986:     /* read and change the sector dirty status */
987:     if (result == FDB_NO_ERR
988:             && _fdb_read_status((fdb_db_t)db, dirty_status_addr, status_table, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_STATUS_NUM) == FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_FALSE) {
989:         result = _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, dirty_status_addr, status_table, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_STATUS_NUM, FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_TRUE, true);
990: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
991:         {
992:             kv_sec_info_t sector_cache = get_sector_from_cache(db, FDB_ALIGN_DOWN(old_kv->addr.start, db_sec_size(db)));
993:             if (sector_cache) {
994:                 sector_cache->status.dirty = FDB_SECTOR_DIRTY_TRUE;
995:             }
996:         }
997: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
998:     }
999: 
1000:     return result;
1001: }

1003: /*
1004:  * move the KV to new space
1005:  */
1006: static fdb_err_t move_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, fdb_kv_t kv)
1007: {
1008:     fdb_err_t result = FDB_NO_ERR;
1009:     uint8_t status_table[KV_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
1010:     uint32_t kv_addr;
1011:     struct kvdb_sec_info sector;
1012: 
1013:     /* prepare to delete the current KV */
1014:     if (kv->status == FDB_KV_WRITE) {
1015:         del_kv(db, NULL, kv, false);
1016:     }
1017: 
1018:     if ((kv_addr = alloc_kv(db, &sector, kv->len)) != FAILED_ADDR) {
1019:         if (db->in_recovery_check && kv->status == FDB_KV_PRE_DELETE) {
1020:             struct fdb_kv kv_bak;
1021:             char name[FDB_KV_NAME_MAX + 1] = { 0 };
1022:             strncpy(name, kv->name, kv->name_len);
1023:             /* check the KV in flash is already create success */
1024:             if (find_kv_no_cache(db, name, &kv_bak)) {
1025:                 /* already create success, don't need to duplicate */
1026:                 result = FDB_NO_ERR;
1027:                 goto __exit;
1028:             }
1029:         }
1030:     } else {
1031:         return FDB_SAVED_FULL;
1032:     }
1033:     /* start move the KV */
1034:     {
1035:         uint8_t buf[32];
1036:         size_t len, size, kv_len = kv->len;
1037: 
1038:         /* update the new KV sector status first */
1039:         update_sec_status(db, &sector, kv->len, NULL);
1040: 
1041:         _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, kv_addr, status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_PRE_WRITE, false);
1042:         kv_len -= KV_MAGIC_OFFSET;
1043:         for (len = 0, size = 0; len < kv_len; len += size) {
1044:             if (len + sizeof(buf) < kv_len) {
1045:                 size = sizeof(buf);
1046:             } else {
1047:                 size = kv_len - len;
1048:             }
1049:             _fdb_flash_read((fdb_db_t)db, kv->addr.start + KV_MAGIC_OFFSET + len, (uint32_t *) buf, FDB_WG_ALIGN(size));
1050:             result = _fdb_flash_write((fdb_db_t)db, kv_addr + KV_MAGIC_OFFSET + len, (uint32_t *) buf, size, true);
1051:         }
1052:         _fdb_write_status((fdb_db_t)db, kv_addr, status_table, FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM, FDB_KV_WRITE, true);
1053: 
1054: #ifdef FDB_KV_USING_CACHE
1055:         update_sector_empty_addr_cache(db, FDB_ALIGN_DOWN(kv_addr, db_sec_size(db)),
1056:                 kv_addr + KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE + FDB_WG_ALIGN(kv->name_len) + FDB_WG_ALIGN(kv->value_len));
1057:         update_kv_cache(db, kv->name, kv->name_len, kv_addr);
1058: #endif /* FDB_KV_USING_CACHE */
1059:     }
1060: 
1061:     FDB_DEBUG("Moved the KV (%.*s) from 0x%08" PRIX32 " to 0x%08" PRIX32 ".\n", kv->name_len, kv->name, kv->addr.start, kv_addr);
1062: 
1063: __exit:
1064:     del_kv(db, NULL, kv, true);
1065: 
1066:     return result;
1067: }

1069: static uint32_t new_kv(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, size_t kv_size)
1070: {
1071:     bool already_gc = false;
1072:     uint32_t empty_kv = FAILED_ADDR;
1073: 
1074: __retry:
1075: 
1076:     if ((empty_kv = alloc_kv(db, sector, kv_size)) == FAILED_ADDR) {
1077:         if (db->gc_request && !already_gc) {
1078:             FDB_DEBUG("Alloc an KV (size %" PRIu32 ") failed when new KV. Now will GC then retry.\n", (uint32_t)kv_size);
1079:             gc_collect_by_free_size(db, kv_size);
1080:             already_gc = true;
1081:             goto __retry;
1082:         } else if (already_gc) {
1083:             FDB_INFO("Error: Alloc an KV (size %" PRIuLEAST16 ") failed after GC. KV full.\n", kv_size);
1084:             db->gc_request = false;
1085:         }
1086:     }
1087: 
1088:     return empty_kv;
1089: }

1091: static uint32_t new_kv_ex(fdb_kvdb_t db, kv_sec_info_t sector, size_t key_len, size_t buf_len)
1092: {
1093:     size_t kv_len = KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE + FDB_WG_ALIGN(key_len) + FDB_WG_ALIGN(buf_len);
1094: 
1095:     return new_kv(db, sector, kv_len);

1098: static bool gc_check_cb(kv_sec_info_t sector, void *arg1, void *arg2)
1099: {
1100:     size_t *empty_sec_num = arg1;
1101:     uint32_t *empty_sec_addr = arg2;
1102: 
1103:     if (sector->check_ok) {
1104:         *empty_sec_num = *empty_sec_num + 1;
1105:         *empty_sec_addr = sector->addr;
1106:     }
1107: 
1108:     return false;
1109: 
1110: }
