363:     /// Write a TSL.
364:     fn write_tsl(&mut self, blob: &[u8], time: FdbTime) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
365:         let idx_data_sz = log_idx_data_size();
366:         let idx_addr = self.cur_sec.empty_idx;
367:         let log_addr = self.cur_sec.empty_data - wg_align(blob.len()) as u32;
368: 
369:         // Build index data
370:         let ts_off = log_idx_ts_offset();
371:         let mut idx_buf = vec![FDB_BYTE_ERASED; idx_data_sz];
372:         // Status will be written separately
373:         // Write time
374:         idx_buf[ts_off..ts_off + 4].copy_from_slice(&time.to_le_bytes());
375:         // Write log_len
376:         idx_buf[ts_off + 4..ts_off + 8].copy_from_slice(&(blob.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
377:         // Write log_addr
378:         idx_buf[ts_off + 8..ts_off + 12].copy_from_slice(&log_addr.to_le_bytes());
379: 
380:         // Write pre-write status
381:         let mut st = vec![0u8; TSL_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
382:         status::write_status(self.be(), idx_addr, &mut st, FDB_TSL_STATUS_NUM, TslStatus::PreWrite as usize, false)?;
383: 
384:         // Write rest of index
385:         self.be().write(idx_addr + ts_off as u32, &idx_buf[ts_off..], false)?;
386: 
387:         // Write blob data
388:         status::write_align(self.be(), log_addr, blob)?;
389: 
390:         // Write WRITE status
391:         let mut st = vec![0u8; TSL_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
392:         status::write_status(self.be(), idx_addr, &mut st, FDB_TSL_STATUS_NUM, TslStatus::Write as usize, true)?;
393: 
394:         Ok(())
395:     }
396: 
397:     /// Update sector status for TSL append.
398:     fn update_sec_status(&mut self, blob_len: usize, cur_time: FdbTime) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
399:         let idx_data_sz = log_idx_data_size();
400:         let aligned_blob = wg_align(blob_len);
401:         let needed = idx_data_sz + aligned_blob;
402: 
403:         if self.cur_sec.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using && self.cur_sec.remain < needed {
404:             // Sector is full, save end info
405:             let end_index_temp = self.cur_sec.empty_idx - idx_data_sz as u32;
406:             let cur_sec_addr = self.cur_sec.addr;
407: 
408:             // Save end info
409:             for slot in 0..2 {
410:                 let (time_off, idx_off, status_off) = if slot == 0 {
411:                     (sector_end0_time_offset(), sector_end0_idx_offset(), sector_end0_status_offset())
412:                 } else {
413:                     (sector_end1_time_offset(), sector_end1_idx_offset(), sector_end1_status_offset())
414:                 };
415: 
416:                 if self.cur_sec.end_info_stat[slot] == TslStatus::Unused {
417:                     let mut st = vec![0u8; TSL_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
418:                     status::write_status(self.be(), cur_sec_addr + status_off as u32, &mut st, FDB_TSL_STATUS_NUM, TslStatus::PreWrite as usize, false)?;
419:                     let mut time_buf = vec![FDB_BYTE_ERASED; wg_align(4)];
420:                     time_buf[..4].copy_from_slice(&self.last_time.to_le_bytes());
421:                     self.be().write(cur_sec_addr + time_off as u32, &time_buf, false)?;
422:                     let mut idx_buf = vec![FDB_BYTE_ERASED; wg_align(4)];
423:                     idx_buf[..4].copy_from_slice(&end_index_temp.to_le_bytes());
424:                     self.be().write(cur_sec_addr + idx_off as u32, &idx_buf, false)?;
425:                     let mut st = vec![0u8; TSL_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
426:                     status::write_status(self.be(), cur_sec_addr + status_off as u32, &mut st, FDB_TSL_STATUS_NUM, TslStatus::Write as usize, true)?;
427:                     break;
428:                 }
429:             }
430: 
431:             // Change sector to FULL
432:             let mut st = vec![0u8; FDB_STORE_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
433:             status::write_status(self.be(), cur_sec_addr, &mut st, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM, SectorStoreStatus::Full as usize, true)?;
434:             self.cur_sec.status = SectorStoreStatus::Full;
435: 
436:             // Find next sector
437:             let new_sec_addr = if cur_sec_addr + self.sec_size < self.max_size {
438:                 cur_sec_addr + self.sec_size
439:             } else if self.rollover {
440:                 0
441:             } else {
442:                 return Err(FdbErr::SavedFull);
443:             };
444: 
445:             self.read_sector_info_inner(new_sec_addr, false)?;
446:             if self.cur_sec.status != SectorStoreStatus::Empty {
447:                 self.oldest_addr = if new_sec_addr + self.sec_size < self.max_size {
448:                     new_sec_addr + self.sec_size
449:                 } else {
450:                     0
451:                 };
452:                 self.format_sector(new_sec_addr)?;
453:                 self.read_sector_info_inner(new_sec_addr, false)?;
454:             }
455:         } else if self.cur_sec.status == SectorStoreStatus::Full {
456:             return Err(FdbErr::SavedFull);
457:         }
458: 
459:         if self.cur_sec.status == SectorStoreStatus::Empty {
460:             self.cur_sec.status = SectorStoreStatus::Using;
461:             self.cur_sec.start_time = cur_time;
462:             let mut st = vec![0u8; FDB_STORE_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE];
463:             status::write_status(self.be(), self.cur_sec.addr, &mut st, FDB_SECTOR_STORE_STATUS_NUM, SectorStoreStatus::Using as usize, true)?;
464: 
465:             let mut time_buf = vec![FDB_BYTE_ERASED; wg_align(4)];
466:             time_buf[..4].copy_from_slice(&cur_time.to_le_bytes());
467:             self.be().write(self.cur_sec.addr + sector_start_time_offset() as u32, &time_buf, true)?;
468:         }
469: 
470:         Ok(())
471:     }
472: 
473:     fn read_sector_info_inner(&mut self, addr: u32, traversal: bool) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
474:         let sector = self.read_sector_info(addr, traversal)?;
475:         self.cur_sec = sector;
476:         Ok(())
477:     }

479:     /// Append a TSL.
480:     fn tsl_append(&mut self, blob: &[u8], timestamp: Option<FdbTime>) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
481:         let cur_time = match timestamp {
482:             Some(t) => t,
483:             None => (self.get_time_fn.unwrap())(),
484:         };
485: 
486:         if blob.len() > self.max_len {
487:             return Err(FdbErr::WriteErr);
488:         }
489: 
490:         if cur_time <= self.last_time {
491:             return Err(FdbErr::WriteErr);
492:         }
493: 
494:         self.update_sec_status(blob.len(), cur_time)?;
495:         self.write_tsl(blob, cur_time)?;
496: 
497:         // Update current sector info
498:         self.cur_sec.end_idx = self.cur_sec.empty_idx;
499:         self.cur_sec.end_time = cur_time;
500:         self.cur_sec.empty_idx += log_idx_data_size() as u32;
501:         self.cur_sec.empty_data -= wg_align(blob.len()) as u32;
502:         self.cur_sec.remain -= log_idx_data_size() + wg_align(blob.len());
503:         self.last_time = cur_time;
504: 
505:         Ok(())
506:     }

508:     /// Format all sectors.
509:     fn tsl_format_all(&mut self) {
510:         let mut sector = TsdbSecInfo::default();
511:         sector.addr = 0;
512: 
513:         let mut sec_addr = 0u32;
514:         let mut traversed_len = 0u32;
515:         loop {
516:             traversed_len += self.sec_size;
517:             let _ = self.format_sector(sec_addr);
518:             let next = self.get_next_sector_addr(&{
519:                 let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
520:                 s.addr = sec_addr;
521:                 s
522:             }, traversed_len);
523:             if next == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
524:             sec_addr = next;
525:         }
526: 
527:         self.oldest_addr = 0;
528:         self.cur_sec = TsdbSecInfo::default();
529:         self.cur_sec.addr = 0;
530:         self.last_time = 0;
531: 
532:         let _ = self.read_sector_info_inner(0, false);
533:     }

537:     pub fn init(&mut self, name: &str, path: &str, get_time: fn() -> FdbTime, max_len: usize, user_data: *mut core::ffi::c_void) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
538:         self.name = name.to_string();
539:         self.dir = path.to_string();
540:         self.user_data = user_data;
541: 
542:         if self.init_ok {
543:             return Ok(());
544:         }
545: 
546:         if self.file_mode {
547:             let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(path);
548:         }
549: 
550:         if self.sec_size == 0 || self.max_size == 0 {
551:             return Err(FdbErr::InitFailed);
552:         }
553: 
554:         if self.max_size % self.sec_size != 0 {
555:             return Err(FdbErr::InitFailed);
556:         }
557:         if self.max_size / self.sec_size < 2 {
558:             return Err(FdbErr::InitFailed);
559:         }
560: 
561:         self.backend = Some(Box::new(crate::FileBackend::new(name, path, self.sec_size, self.max_size)));
562: 
563:         self.db_lock();
564: 
565:         self.get_time_fn = Some(get_time);
566:         self.max_len = max_len;
567:         self.rollover = true;
568:         self.oldest_addr = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
569:         self.cur_sec = TsdbSecInfo::default();
570:         self.cur_sec.addr = FDB_DATA_UNUSED;
571: 
572:         // Check all sector headers
573:         let mut check_failed = false;
574:         let mut empty_num = 0usize;
575:         let mut empty_addr = 0u32;
576:         let mut cur_sec_found = false;
577: 
578:         let mut sec_addr = 0u32;
579:         let mut traversed_len = 0u32;
580:         loop {
581:             traversed_len += self.sec_size;
582:             match self.read_sector_info(sec_addr, true) {
583:                 Ok(sector) => {
584:                     if !sector.check_ok {
585:                         check_failed = true;
586:                     } else if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using {
587:                         if self.cur_sec.addr == FDB_DATA_UNUSED {
588:                             self.cur_sec = sector;
589:                             cur_sec_found = true;
590:                         } else {
591:                             check_failed = true;
592:                         }
593:                     } else if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Empty {
594:                         empty_num += 1;
595:                         empty_addr = sector.addr;
596:                         if empty_num == 1 && self.cur_sec.addr == FDB_DATA_UNUSED {
597:                             self.cur_sec = sector;
598:                         }
599:                     }
600:                 }
601:                 Err(_) => {
602:                     check_failed = true;
603:                 }
604:             }
605:             let next = {
606:                 let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
607:                 s.addr = sec_addr;
608:                 s
609:             };
610:             let n = self.get_next_sector_addr(&next, traversed_len);
611:             if n == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
612:             sec_addr = n;
613:         }
614: 
615:         if check_failed {
616:             if self.not_formatable {
617:                 self.db_unlock();
618:                 return Err(FdbErr::ReadErr);
619:             }
620:             self.tsl_format_all();
621:         } else {
622:             let latest_addr = if empty_num > 0 {
623:                 empty_addr
624:             } else if self.rollover {
625:                 self.cur_sec.addr
626:             } else {
627:                 self.cur_sec.addr = self.max_size - self.sec_size;
628:                 self.cur_sec.addr
629:             };
630: 
631:             if latest_addr + self.sec_size >= self.max_size {
632:                 self.oldest_addr = 0;
633:             } else {
634:                 self.oldest_addr = latest_addr + self.sec_size;
635:             }
636:         }
637: 
638:         // Read current using sector info
639:         let _ = self.read_sector_info_inner(self.cur_sec.addr, true);
640: 
641:         // Get last save time
642:         if self.cur_sec.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using {
643:             self.last_time = self.cur_sec.end_time;
644:         } else if self.cur_sec.status == SectorStoreStatus::Empty && self.oldest_addr != self.cur_sec.addr {
645:             let addr = if self.cur_sec.addr == 0 {
646:                 self.max_size - self.sec_size
647:             } else {
648:                 self.cur_sec.addr - self.sec_size
649:             };
650:             if let Ok(sec) = self.read_sector_info(addr, false) {
651:                 self.last_time = sec.end_time;
652:             }
653:         }
654: 
655:         self.db_unlock();
656:         self.init_ok = true;
657: 
658:         Ok(())
659:     }

693:     /// Iterate over all TSLs.
694:     pub fn tsl_iter<F>(&mut self, mut cb: F)
695:     where
696:         F: FnMut(&TslInfo) -> bool,
697:     {
698:         if !self.init_ok {
699:             return;
700:         }
701: 
702:         self.db_lock();
703:         let mut sec_addr = self.oldest_addr;
704:         let mut traversed_len = 0u32;
705: 
706:         loop {
707:             traversed_len += self.sec_size;
708:             let sector = match self.read_sector_info(sec_addr, false) {
709:                 Ok(s) => s,
710:                 Err(_) => {
711:                     let next = {
712:                         let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
713:                         s.addr = sec_addr;
714:                         s
715:                     };
716:                     let n = self.get_next_sector_addr(&next, traversed_len);
717:                     if n == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
718:                     sec_addr = n;
719:                     continue;
720:                 }
721:             };
722: 
723:             if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using || sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Full {
724:                 let sector = if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using {
725:                     self.cur_sec.clone()
726:                 } else {
727:                     sector
728:                 };
729: 
730:                 let mut tsl = TslInfo::default();
731:                 tsl.addr.index = sector.addr + sector_hdr_data_size() as u32;
732:                 loop {
733:                     if self.read_tsl(&mut tsl).is_err() { break; }
734:                     if cb(&tsl) {
735:                         self.db_unlock();
736:                         return;
737:                     }
738:                     let next = self.get_next_tsl_addr(&sector, &tsl);
739:                     if next == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
740:                     tsl.addr.index = next;
741:                 }
742:             }
743: 
744:             let next = {
745:                 let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
746:                 s.addr = sec_addr;
747:                 s
748:             };
749:             let n = self.get_next_sector_addr(&next, traversed_len);
750:             if n == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
751:             sec_addr = n;
752:         }
753: 
754:         self.db_unlock();
755:     }

757:     /// Iterate over TSLs in reverse.
758:     pub fn tsl_iter_reverse<F>(&mut self, mut cb: F)
759:     where
760:         F: FnMut(&TslInfo) -> bool,
761:     {
762:         if !self.init_ok {
763:             return;
764:         }
765: 
766:         self.db_lock();
767:         let mut sec_addr = self.cur_sec.addr;
768:         let mut traversed_len = 0u32;
769: 
770:         loop {
771:             traversed_len += self.sec_size;
772:             let sector = match self.read_sector_info(sec_addr, false) {
773:                 Ok(s) => s,
774:                 Err(_) => {
775:                     let next = {
776:                         let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
777:                         s.addr = sec_addr;
778:                         s
779:                     };
780:                     let n = self.get_last_sector_addr(&next, traversed_len);
781:                     if n == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
782:                     sec_addr = n;
783:                     continue;
784:                 }
785:             };
786: 
787:             if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using || sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Full {
788:                 let sector = if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Using {
789:                     self.cur_sec.clone()
790:                 } else {
791:                     sector
792:                 };
793: 
794:                 let mut tsl = TslInfo::default();
795:                 tsl.addr.index = sector.end_idx;
796:                 loop {
797:                     if self.read_tsl(&mut tsl).is_err() { break; }
798:                     if cb(&tsl) {
799:                         self.db_unlock();
800:                         return;
801:                     }
802:                     let prev = self.get_last_tsl_addr(&sector, &tsl);
803:                     if prev == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
804:                     tsl.addr.index = prev;
805:                 }
806:             } else if sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Empty || sector.status == SectorStoreStatus::Unused {
807:                 break;
808:             }
809: 
810:             let next = {
811:                 let mut s = TsdbSecInfo::default();
812:                 s.addr = sec_addr;
813:                 s
814:             };
815:             let n = self.get_last_sector_addr(&next, traversed_len);
816:             if n == FDB_FAILED_ADDR { break; }
817:             sec_addr = n;
818:         }
819: 
820:         self.db_unlock();
821:     }

823:     /// Binary search for start TSL address.
824:     fn search_start_tsl_addr(&mut self, start: u32, end: u32, from: FdbTime, to: FdbTime) -> u32 {
825:         let mut start = start;
826:         let mut end = end;
827:         let idx_data_sz = log_idx_data_size() as u32;
828: 
829:         loop {
830:             let mid = start + fdb_align_down(((end - start) / 2) as usize, log_idx_data_size()) as u32;
831:             let mut tsl = TslInfo::default();
832:             tsl.addr.index = mid;
833:             let _ = self.read_tsl(&mut tsl);
834: 
835:             if tsl.time < from {
836:                 start = tsl.addr.index + idx_data_sz;
837:             } else if tsl.time > from {
838:                 end = tsl.addr.index - idx_data_sz;
839:             } else {
840:                 return tsl.addr.index;
841:             }
842: 
843:             if start > end {
844:                 if from > to {
845:                     let mut tsl = TslInfo::default();
846:                     tsl.addr.index = start;
847:                     let _ = self.read_tsl(&mut tsl);
848:                     if tsl.time > from {
849:                         start -= idx_data_sz;
850:                     }
851:                 }
852:                 break;
853:             }
854:         }
855: 
856:         start
857:     }

859:     /// Iterate TSLs by time range.
860:     pub fn tsl_iter_by_time<F>(&mut self, from: FdbTime, to: FdbTime, mut cb: F)
861:     where

39: /// Identical semantics to C `_fdb_get_status`.
40: pub fn get_status(status_table: &[u8], status_num: usize) -> usize {
41:     let mut i = 0usize;
42:     let mut status_num_bak = status_num;
43:     let sn = status_num - 1;
44:     status_num_bak = sn + 1;
45: 
46:     let mut count = sn;
47:     loop {
48:         if count == 0 {
49:             break;
50:         }
51:         if FDB_WRITE_GRAN == 1 {
52:             if (status_table[count / 8] & (0x80 >> (count % 8)) as u8) == 0x00 {
53:                 break;
54:             }
55:         } else {
56:             if status_table[count * FDB_WRITE_GRAN / 8] == FDB_BYTE_WRITTEN {
57:                 break;
58:             }
59:         }
60:         i += 1;
61:         if count == 0 { break; }
62:         count -= 1;
63:     }
64: 
65:     status_num_bak - i
66: }
67: 
68: /// Write a status to flash via the backend.
69: /// Identical semantics to C `_fdb_write_status`.
70: pub fn write_status(
71:     backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
72:     addr: u32,
73:     status_table: &mut [u8],
74:     status_num: usize,
75:     status_index: usize,
76:     sync: bool,
77: ) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
78:     assert!(status_index < status_num);
79: 
80:     let byte_index = set_status(status_table, status_num, status_index);
81: 
82:     if byte_index == usize::MAX {
83:         return Ok(());
84:     }
85: 
86:     if FDB_WRITE_GRAN == 1 {
87:         backend.write(addr + byte_index as u32, &status_table[byte_index..byte_index + 1], sync)
88:     } else {
89:         let gran_bytes = FDB_WRITE_GRAN / 8;
90:         backend.write(addr + byte_index as u32, &status_table[byte_index..byte_index + gran_bytes], sync)
91:     }
92: }
93: 
94: /// Read a status from flash via the backend.
95: /// Returns the status index.
96: /// Identical semantics to C `_fdb_read_status`.
97: pub fn read_status(
98:     backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
99:     addr: u32,
100:     status_table: &mut [u8],
101:     total_num: usize,
102: ) -> usize {
103:     let table_size = status_table_size(total_num);
104:     if backend.read(addr, &mut status_table[..table_size]).is_err() {
105:         // If read fails, treat as all-erased
106:         for b in status_table.iter_mut().take(table_size) {
107:             *b = FDB_BYTE_ERASED;
108:         }
109:     }
110:     get_status(status_table, total_num)
111: }
112: 
113: /// Find the continue 0xFF flash address.
114: /// Identical semantics to C `_fdb_continue_ff_addr`.
115: pub fn continue_ff_addr(
116:     backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
117:     start: u32,
118:     end: u32,
119:     sec_size: u32,
120: ) -> u32 {
121:     let mut buf = [0u8; 32];
122:     let mut last_data = FDB_BYTE_WRITTEN;
123:     let mut addr = start;
124:     let mut cur = start;
125: 
126:     while cur < end {
127:         let read_size = if cur + 32 < end { 32 } else { (end - cur) as usize };
128:         if backend.read(cur, &mut buf[..read_size]).is_err() {
129:             break;
130:         }
131:         for i in 0..read_size {
132:             if last_data != FDB_BYTE_ERASED && buf[i] == FDB_BYTE_ERASED {
133:                 addr = cur + i as u32;
134:             }
135:             last_data = buf[i];
136:         }
137:         cur += 32;
138:     }
139: 
140:     if last_data == FDB_BYTE_ERASED {
141:         wg_align(addr as usize) as u32
142:     } else {
143:         end
144:     }
145: }
146: 
147: /// Write data aligned to write granularity.
148: /// Identical semantics to C `_fdb_flash_write_align`.
149: pub fn write_align(
150:     backend: &mut dyn StorageBackend,
151:     addr: u32,
152:     data: &[u8],
153: ) -> Result<(), FdbErr> {
154:     let aligned_down = crate::wg_align_down(data.len());
155:     if aligned_down > 0 {
156:         backend.write(addr, &data[..aligned_down], false)?;
157:     }
158: 
159:     let remain = data.len() - aligned_down;
160:     if remain > 0 {
161:         let unit = crate::wg_unit();
162:         let mut align_data = vec![FDB_BYTE_ERASED; unit];
163:         align_data[..remain].copy_from_slice(&data[aligned_down..aligned_down + remain]);
164:         backend.write(addr + aligned_down as u32, &align_data, false)?;
165:     }
166: 
167:     Ok(())
168: }

> **Note**: This project is forked from [armink/FlashDB](https://gitee.com/armink/FlashDB) for practicing high-performance programming. Non-Linux platform code (STM32, ESP32/8266, Zephyr demos and ports) has been removed, and Linux unit tests and performance benchmarks have been added.

## Introduction

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) is a lightweight Flash database that focuses on providing data storage solutions for IoT and embedded products. Different from traditional database based on file system, [FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) combines the features of Flash and has strong performance and reliability. And under the premise of ensuring extremely low resource occupation, the service life of Flash should be extended as much as possible.

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) provides two database modes:

- **Key-value database**: It is a non-relational database that stores data as a collection of key-value pairs, where the key is used as a unique identifier. KVDB has simple operation and strong scalability.
- **Time Series Database**: Time Series Database (TSDB), which stores data in **time sequence**. TSDB data has a timestamp, a large amount of data storage, and high insertion and query performance.

## Usage scenario

FlashDB provides a variety of data storage solutions, not only has a small resource footprint, but also has a large storage capacity, which is very suitable for IoT products. The following are the main application scenarios:

- **Key-value database**:
  - Product parameter storage
  - User configuration information storage
  - Small file management
- **Time Series Database**: 
  - Store dynamically generated structured data: such as environmental monitoring information collected by temperature and humidity sensors, human health information recorded in real time by smart bracelets, etc.
  - Record operation log: store operation log of product history, record of abnormal alarm, etc.

## Key Features

- Very small footprint, ram usage is almost **0**;
- Support multiple partitions, **multiple instances**. When the amount of data is large, the partition can be refined to reduce the retrieval time;
- Support **wear balance** to extend Flash life;
- Support **Power-off protection** function, high reliability;
- Supports two KV types, string and blob, which is convenient for users to operate;
- Support KV **incremental upgrade**, after product firmware upgrade, KVDB content also supports automatic upgrade;
- Support to modify the status of each TSDB record to facilitate user management;
- Support POSIX file mode for Linux and other POSIX platforms;

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Path             | Storage Type |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------ |
| linux    | `demos/linux`    | posix file   |

## How to use

FlashDB provides comprehensive documentation, see: https://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/

Quick access:

- [API Document](http://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/api)

/**
 * @file

#include "test_helpers.h"
#include <flashdb.h>
#include <fdb_low_lvl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <inttypes.h>

#include <unistd.h>

#define TEST_TS_PART_NAME             "fdb_kvdb1"
#define TEST_KV_BLOB_NAME             "kv_blob_test"
#define TEST_KV_NAME                  "kv_test"

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Dynamically compute TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN so that exactly 3 KVs fit
 * per TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_SIZE-byte sector for ANY FDB_WRITE_GRAN value,
 * AND so that the test_fdb_gc2 GC path works correctly.
 *
 * Let:
 *   B       = _TKV_BASE  = KV_HDR_SZ + aligned_name
 *   V       = TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN  (aligned to W)
 *   kv_size = B + V
 *   kv5_size= B + 2V  (kv5 value = 2×V)
 *   kv4_size= B + 3V  (kv4 value = 3×V)
 *   th      = _TKV_THRESHOLD = KV_HDR_SZ + FDB_KV_NAME_MAX
 *   usable  = TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_SIZE - _TKV_SEC_HDR_SZ
 *
 * Three constraints, from LEAST to MOST strict:
 *
 *  [A] 4th KV does NOT fit (exactly 3 per sector):
 *      V >= ceil((usable - 5B - 64) / 4)
 *
 *  [B] kv4 (3×V) occupies a full sector (no normal KV fits after it):
 *      usable - (B+3V) <= (B+V) + th
 *      V >= ceil((usable - 3B - 64) / 4)
 *
 *  [C] GC does NOT stop early when kv1+kv2 are moved into the initially
 *      empty sector (sector3).  do_gc() stops when remain > free_size,
 *      where free_size = kv5_size = B+2V.  We need:
 *        usable - 2*(B+V)  <=  B + 2V
 *        3984 - 3B  <=  4V
 *      V >= ceil((usable - 3B) / 4)   ← STRICTEST BOUND (no -64 term)
 *
 * All three constraints reduce to the same form; [C] dominates.
 * The minimum V satisfying [C] (ceiling integer division: (N+3)/4):
 *
 *   V_min = FDB_WG_ALIGN( (usable - 3B + 3) / 4 )
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* write-gran alignment unit in bytes */
#define _TKV_W                    ((FDB_WRITE_GRAN + 7) / 8)

/* KV status table size */
#define _TKV_KV_STATUS_SZ         FDB_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE(FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM)

/* Sector header raw size (store_status + dirty_status + magic + combined + reserved) */
#define _TKV_SEC_HDR_RAW_SZ       (FDB_STORE_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE + FDB_DIRTY_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE \
                                   + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t))
#define _TKV_SEC_HDR_SZ           FDB_WG_ALIGN(_TKV_SEC_HDR_RAW_SZ)

/* KV header raw size (status + magic + len + crc32 + name_len + value_len) */
#define _TKV_KV_HDR_RAW_SZ        (_TKV_KV_STATUS_SZ + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) \
                                   + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint8_t) + sizeof(uint32_t))
#define _TKV_KV_HDR_SZ            FDB_WG_ALIGN(_TKV_KV_HDR_RAW_SZ)

/* FDB_SEC_REMAIN_THRESHOLD equivalent: KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE + FDB_KV_NAME_MAX */
#define _TKV_THRESHOLD            (_TKV_KV_HDR_SZ + FDB_KV_NAME_MAX)

/* name length of "kv0".."kv5", aligned */
#define _TKV_NAME_ALIGNED         FDB_WG_ALIGN(3)

/* usable data space per sector */
#define _TKV_USABLE               (TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_SIZE - _TKV_SEC_HDR_SZ)

/* per-KV base overhead: header + aligned name */
#define _TKV_BASE                 (_TKV_KV_HDR_SZ + _TKV_NAME_ALIGNED)

/* Minimum V satisfying constraint [C] (the strictest).
 * Uses ceiling integer division: (N + 3) / 4. */
#define _TKV_MAX_VAL_ALIGNED      FDB_WG_ALIGN((_TKV_USABLE - 3 * _TKV_BASE + 3) / 4)

/* TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN: use aligned size directly (already a multiple of W) */
#define TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN         _TKV_MAX_VAL_ALIGNED

#define TEST_KV_MAX_NUM                8
#define TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_SIZE          4096
#define TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_NUM           4

#define FDB_ARRAY_SIZE(array)          (sizeof(array) / sizeof(array[0]))

#include <flashdb.h>
#include <fdb_low_lvl.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <inttypes.h>

#define TEST_KV_BLOB_NAME             "kv_blob_test"
#define TEST_KV_NAME                  "kv_test"

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Dynamically compute TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN so that exactly 3 KVs fit
 * per TEST_KVDB_SECTOR_SIZE-byte sector for ANY FDB_WRITE_GRAN value,
 * AND so that the test_fdb_gc2 GC path works correctly.

 *   V       = TEST_KV_VALUE_LEN  (aligned to W)
 *   kv_size = B + V

 *

 *      empty sector (sector3).  do_gc() stops when remain > free_size,
 *      where free_size = kv5_size = B+2V.  We need:
 *        usable - 2*(B+V)  <=  B + 2V
 *        3984 - 3B  <=  4V
 *      V >= ceil((usable - 3B) / 4)   ← STRICTEST BOUND (no -64 term)
 *
 * All three constraints reduce to the same form; [C] dominates.
 * The minimum V satisfying [C] (ceiling integer division: (N+3)/4):
 *
 *   V_min = FDB_WG_ALIGN( (usable - 3B + 3) / 4 )
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------*/

/* write-gran alignment unit in bytes */
#define _TKV_W                    ((FDB_WRITE_GRAN + 7) / 8)

/* KV status table size */
#define _TKV_KV_STATUS_SZ         FDB_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE(FDB_KV_STATUS_NUM)

/* Sector header raw size (store_status + dirty_status + magic + combined + reserved) */
#define _TKV_SEC_HDR_RAW_SZ       (FDB_STORE_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE + FDB_DIRTY_STATUS_TABLE_SIZE \
                                   + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t))
#define _TKV_SEC_HDR_SZ           FDB_WG_ALIGN(_TKV_SEC_HDR_RAW_SZ)

/* KV header raw size (status + magic + len + crc32 + name_len + value_len) */
#define _TKV_KV_HDR_RAW_SZ        (_TKV_KV_STATUS_SZ + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) \
                                   + sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint8_t) + sizeof(uint32_t))
#define _TKV_KV_HDR_SZ            FDB_WG_ALIGN(_TKV_KV_HDR_RAW_SZ)

/* FDB_SEC_REMAIN_THRESHOLD equivalent: KV_HDR_DATA_SIZE + FDB_KV_NAME_MAX */
#define _TKV_THRESHOLD            (_TKV_KV_HDR_SZ + FDB_KV_NAME_MAX)

> **Note**: This project is forked from [armink/FlashDB](https://gitee.com/armink/FlashDB) for practicing high-performance programming. Non-Linux platform code (STM32, ESP32/8266, Zephyr demos and ports) has been removed, and Linux unit tests and performance benchmarks have been added.

## Introduction

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) is a lightweight Flash database that focuses on providing data storage solutions for IoT and embedded products. Different from traditional database based on file system, [FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) combines the features of Flash and has strong performance and reliability. And under the premise of ensuring extremely low resource occupation, the service life of Flash should be extended as much as possible.

[FlashDB](https://github.com/armink/FlashDB) provides two database modes:

- **Key-value database**: It is a non-relational database that stores data as a collection of key-value pairs, where the key is used as a unique identifier. KVDB has simple operation and strong scalability.
- **Time Series Database**: Time Series Database (TSDB), which stores data in **time sequence**. TSDB data has a timestamp, a large amount of data storage, and high insertion and query performance.

## Usage scenario

FlashDB provides a variety of data storage solutions, not only has a small resource footprint, but also has a large storage capacity, which is very suitable for IoT products. The following are the main application scenarios:

- **Key-value database**:
  - Product parameter storage
  - User configuration information storage
  - Small file management
- **Time Series Database**: 
  - Store dynamically generated structured data: such as environmental monitoring information collected by temperature and humidity sensors, human health information recorded in real time by smart bracelets, etc.
  - Record operation log: store operation log of product history, record of abnormal alarm, etc.

## Key Features

- Very small footprint, ram usage is almost **0**;
- Support multiple partitions, **multiple instances**. When the amount of data is large, the partition can be refined to reduce the retrieval time;
- Support **wear balance** to extend Flash life;
- Support **Power-off protection** function, high reliability;
- Supports two KV types, string and blob, which is convenient for users to operate;
- Support KV **incremental upgrade**, after product firmware upgrade, KVDB content also supports automatic upgrade;
- Support to modify the status of each TSDB record to facilitate user management;
- Support POSIX file mode for Linux and other POSIX platforms;

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Path             | Storage Type |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------ |
| linux    | `demos/linux`    | posix file   |

## How to use

FlashDB provides comprehensive documentation, see: https://armink.github.io/FlashDB/#/
